data.Contenuti: Main methods and models of statistical learning for modeling and understanding complex datasets, with a focus on supervised learning, with regression and classification methods. Contents include extensions of linear regression model, polynomial regression, logistic regression, and linear discriminant analysis; models for categorical data; resampling methods (cross-validation and bootstrap), linear model selection and regularization methods (subset selection, shrinkage methods, dimension reduction methods); nonlinear models, splines and generalized additive models. Computing is done in R, with possible integration of data analysis software that utilizes the R environment for statistical computing, through tutorial sessions and homework assignments. Case studies and applications focus on digital economy and management.
data.Testi: Course materials and lecture slides available on the e-learning platform.An introduction to Statistical Learning, 2nd edition, James G., Witten D., Hastie T., Tibshirani R., Springer, 2021, ISBN 9781461471370, https://hastie.su.domains/ISLR2/ISLRv2_website.pdf
data.Obiettivi formativi: The educational objectives are consistent with those characterizing the degree program in “Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management” in which the course is inserted. The course is concerned with the development, use and discussion of the main statistical methods of models of statistical learning useful for the analysis of complex data, to develop evidence-based answers to relevant questions and then give a valid support to strategic decisions in the fields of economics, marketing, management control, business intelligence and social sciences.Case studies and applications are proposed in socioeconomics and management fields, with the final aim of learning how to react to challenges of big data and data-driven economy. Using real cases and applications, the course aims at providing operational and practical guidance to data science, useful to those who, in various corporate functions as well as in public institutions, are involved in collecting, analyzing, processing and evaluating qualitative and quantitative information related to socioeconomic and company data. In detail, students will gain the following skills:1) Knowledge and understanding: by means of a gradual learning process, linking the contents of this course with the educational objectives of the cycle degree program in which the course is inserted, students will acquire the methodological and applied knowledge about the main concepts of statistical learning and will be able to apply such knowledge by means of appropriate software.2) Applying knowledge and understanding: students will be able to implement statistical regression and classification models in order to extract proper information from data, useful to analyse real phenomena in several fields of economics and management, and to understand their most important aspects.3) Making judgements: students who successfully complete this course will be able to select the most appropriate statistical models, apply sound statistical methods, perform the analyses using statistical software, and organize results in order to draw conclusions and decide in uncertain situations, like in specific economic and business situations.4) Communication skills: students who successfully complete this course will be able to communicate, to experts and non-experts, data information and evaluations, also with the help of outputs from specific software and data visualization devices.5) Learning skills: the course is aimed to provide the methodological and applied knowledge of statistical learning, necessary to address subsequent studies, in particular the advanced courses in mathematics, statistics, computer science, the quantitative aspects of economics courses, the applied projects in laboratories and internships, the empirical analyses in the final thesis.
data.Prerequisiti: Descriptive and inferential statistics, basic knowledge of R programming.
data.Metodi didattici: Lessons and practicals with use of computer
data.Altro: If the computer lab cannot be used, students are required to bring their own laptops
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The exam covers all the topics in the Program and consists of two parts:(1) an online test on the Moodle e-learning platform including one open-ended and 5 closed-ended questions concerning theoretical topics and/or short applications of the studied methods; the overall grade of this test amounts to 16 maximum (6 for the open-ended question and 2 for each of the closed-ended questions);(2) a poster exam, consisting in a 5-minute presentation of a poster showing the results of a group project of data analysis using R, followed by an individual oral exam. In detail, a group of students prepare the project, the poster and its presentation. Students are graded on the content, organization and design of the poster itself, the oral presentation of the poster and the ability to answer questions on the poster. The grading of the poster exam occurs in two parts: the group grade (max 8) and an individual grade (max 8 points); the latter is based on a brief individual oral examination administered to each student in the poster group. Although students are permitted to “tag-team” the presentation, it is recommendable that each group chooses one person to be responsible for the presentation.Only at the teacher’s discretion, the poster exam can exceptionally be replaced by a computer-based test, carried out in the computer lab, requiring the analysis of one or more data sets using R and the interpretation of the obtained results. Students can carry out this test with the help of the course material.Final Evaluation: The two parts of the exam (online test and poster exam) are each worth 50% of the total score. The final grade is obtained as the sum of the two grades in the two parts. The exam is passed if the final grade is greater than or equal to 18. It will be given a final grade of 30/30 cum laude to the students who achieve a final score equal to 32.There are no differences between attending and non-attending students. The online test is aimed at verifying skill 1 (Knowledge and understanding).The poster exam (or the computer-based test) allows to verify skills 2, 3 and 4 (Applying knowledge and understanding, Making judgements, Communication skills).The skill concerned with autonomous study (5, Learning skills) is indirectly verified, because passing the exam is also made possible by the autonomous execution of exercises suggested by the teacher for homework.

data.Contenuti: The aim of the course is to provide a comprehensive overview of the European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), its principles, its rules, its method of implementation, its risk-based approach and the activity of the institutions it addresses. The analysis will focus on the pivotal concept of "accountability" of data controllers, the real keystone of the brand new legal order on data protection, which specifically requires aware and responsible actors.The presentation of practical cases demonstrating the need to manage data protection compliance within a strict regulatory framework will allow students to practically develop an intuitive sensitivity to data protection compliance as one of the most valuable strategic assets of a company. Data governance consists of the ability to both extract and interpret salient information, but above all to be able to account for one's choices from the design of data processing, in order to minimise the risk of unnecessary or disruptive interference with personal data and privacy.Another objective of the course is to understand the different approaches to regulating data flows held by the EU's foreign trading partners and how the deep conceptual distinction between 'privacy' and 'data protection' still influences them.
data.Testi: Course materials will be reported in class and will be made available through institutional e-elarning repositories
data.Obiettivi formativi: Knowledge and understanding:At the end of the course, students should be able to:- know the principles and concepts applicable to data ownership and processing;- follow continuous engineering innovation in data processing and understand the significant features of relevant technologies such as the application of big data and artificial intelligence technologies in different sectors;- master the tools and institutions compatible with the new legal framework governing data protection.Application of knowledge:At the end of the study programme, students will be able to:- assess the impact of data processing on the rights and freedoms of data subjects;- elaborate and plan different privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default solutions depending on the specific purposes and situations of processing;- communicate and work effectively as an expert in data protection issues.Judgement skills:At the end of the study programme, students will be able to:- apply the rules set out in specific data processing schemes;- recognise the data protection risks within a processing operation and identify appropriate and effective measures to minimise them- prepare original reports and impact assessments of specific data processing simulations.Communication skills:On completion of the programme of study, students will be able to:- develop the ability to communicate in written form through exercises and in oral form through classroom interaction and debate;- use the knowledge and communication of data protection legislation; and- develop the ability to provide legal advice to data controllers and data processors.Learning skills:At the end of the curriculum, students will be able to:- build an analytical toolbox from data protection and privacy legislation;- solve problems in dynamic contexts and develop critical positions.
data.Prerequisiti: Basic knowledge of information technology and private law
data.Metodi didattici: Classroom-taught lesson, attendance recommended
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The exam consists of a written exam, which is compulsory for all students. The questions will focus on the course programme as it is carried out in the teaching materials made available to students. The grade will be expressed in thirtieth.The evaluation criteria are understanding of legal notions of data protection, ability to analyse, mastery of legal vocabulary, ability to connect.
data.Programma esteso: Context and framework of European data protection lawDifferences between right to privacy and right to data protectionFrom the Parent Directive to the Regulation (GDPR)- "personal data"- Special categories of data ("sensitive data")- "data processing"- subjects of data governanceThe principles of the GDPR- lawfulness, fairness and transparency of processing- purpose limitation- data minimisation- accuracy, storage limitation and security- accountability- conditions for lawfulness of processing and special categories of data- security measures- management of data breaches- accountability rules- compliance tools- data protection by design and by default- DPIASupervisory authorities- powers and sanctions- the European Data Protection BoardThe Data Subject's Rights- the right to be informed- the rights of rectification, restriction and objection- the 'right to be forgotten- the rights against automated decision-making, including profiling- respect of individuals' rights- EU-US agreements on data flowsEU Data Strategy 2020- ePrivacy Regulation- the AI RegulationSpecific types of personal data and their protection rules- health data- genetic and biometric data- data processing for research and statistical purposesContemporary challenges in personal data protection:- big data, algorithms and AI- Web 2.0 and social networks- Web 3.0 and IoT- the Big Tech problem

data.Contenuti: The legitimacy of the firms is at stake. The current multidimensional (that is, financial, economic, social and ecologic) crisis clearly shows that the prevailing patterns of production and consumption are unbearable. Therefore, citizens are asking for a deep change of the course. For many companies, corporate social responsibility (CSR) and sustainability are becoming crucial levers to address societal expectations and evolving market requirements.But how can CSR be the key driver for sustainable value creation processes? And how can firms go beyond simple window-dressing or greenwashing policies to really walk the talk and promote innovation capable of avoiding ethical blowbacks by combining market success and social/ecological enhancements?The Course aims to address these questions by providing students with new perspectives, new managerial approaches, and new tools to face the sustainability challenges.
data.Testi: Attending students: Selected readings and further material will be made available by the instructor during the Course. Non-attending students: Rasche A., Morsing M., Moon J. (Eds.), (2017), Corporate Social Responsibility: Strategy, Communication, Governance, Cambridge (UK), Cambridge University Press [9781107535398: paperback format].
data.Obiettivi formativi: Knowledge and understanding and related applicationThe Course aims at clarifying the real meaning of the Corporate SocialResponsibility (CSR) concept and identifying its strategic implications interms of: • sustainability of value creation processes; • need forinnovative managerial paradigms based on stakeholder engagement andcollaboration; • impact on corporate performance evaluation andreporting methodologies.
data.Prerequisiti: Basic knowledge in the management and marketing fields is needed to better understand the topics addressed in the Course, and fully participate in the class discussions and activities.
data.Metodi didattici: The Course is based on an interactive approach thanks to class discussions, case studies, team works, videos, and so on. Furthermore, qualified managers and experts will be involved.
data.Altro: 9 ECTS Course.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: Attending students: written exam. The student assessment will also take into account class participation.Non-attending students: written exam.

data.Contenuti: The course deals with extensions of the classical topics of International Economics. In particular, the focus is on the economy of European integration, analysing through instruments of international economics, the economic development in the Eurozone, the impact of the financial crisis, major changes in policies and European legislation, the potential impact of the Trans-Atlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP), the effect of enlargement of the European Union, as well as the impact of Brexit. Lastly, recent policies and financial instruments set to face the Covid-19 emergency are included in the course. These include the EU Solidarity Fund, the Support to mitigate Unemployment Risks in an Emergency (SURE), and the Recovery Fund. The theoretical part is accompanied by the analysis of recent policy agendas like the von der Leyen Commission's priorities for 2019-2024 and the EU greed deal.
data.Testi: Baldwin, R. and C. Wyplosz, "The Economics of European Integration", Mc Graw Hill Education, Seventh Edition 2022, ISBN-13 978-1526849434; ISBN-10 1526849437Molle W. “European Cohesion Policy”, Routledge, 2007, ISBN-10: 0415438128; ISBN-13: 978-0415438124John B, Berkowitz P., Hardy S., Muravska T. (a cura di) “EU Cohesion Policy: Reassessing performance and direction”, Routledge, First Edition 2016, ISBN-10: 1138224642; ISBN-13: 978-1138224643Bénassy-Quéré A., and di Mauro B.W., Europe in the Time of Covid-19, CEPR Press 2020, ISBN: 978-1-912179-33-6
data.Obiettivi formativi: a) Knowledge and understanding (KN)The aim of the course is to deepen the knowledge of international economics, applying the main concepts previously acquired to understand the process of European integration under an economic and institutional perspective. Students will be able to identify the main steps of European integration, the macroeconomics of monetary integration, micro policies and the macroeconomics of monetary integration. Furthermore, recent policy strategies like the von der Leyen Commission's priorities for 2019-2024, the EU green deal and tools like the EU Solidarity Fund and Support to mitigate Unemployment Risks in an Emergency (SURE) will be discussed.The course is based on the text "The Economics of European Integration" and the material provided by the teacher.b) Applying knowledge and understanding (AKN)Students will be able to face the topics covered in the course developing the empirical skills needed to check for empirical relation between the data. They will learn to search for data online, to develop a research question, and to use basic econometric tools to analyse data and to draw convincing conclusions.c) Making judgements (MJ)The students will have developed the ability to understand and critically interpret the main economic events in the light of the knowledge acquired during the course. They will be able to read and understand specialized articles (for example from voxeu.org) and to make judgements about the economic policy proposals in the public debate.d) Communication skills (CS)The students will be able to communicate using the appropriate lexicon to different interlocutors. They will write and present a team project in class, and they will have to demonstrate to be able to reply to questions made by the teacher and other students.e) Learning skills (LS)The students will reach the ability to learn autonomously complex economic concepts that will allow them to understand specialized news and articles. Furthermore, they will learn academic writing, to work in team in a project with a deadline, and to empirically analyse data.
data.Prerequisiti: International Economics
data.Metodi didattici: 24 lessons (60 hours) by the Professor Nicola Pontarollo
data.Altro: It is required to send an email to book the reception.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: Modalita' di verifica dell'apprendimento: ATTENDING students' final evaluation of knowledge (KN), applied knowledge (AKN), making judgements (MJ), learning (LS) and communication skills (CS) about IE is based on two components:1) written exam will include: theoretical questions, questions on actual policy initiatives and stylized economic facts understandable thanks to the knowledge acquired, the analysis and the production of charts and the analysis of empirical relationships (KN), (AKN), (LS).2) By December, students write a paper on a topic of their choice (from a list provided by the Professor) and present it in class using slides. This is a teamwork, and the teacher sets each team. An evaluation of the work is given to the team and to each individual (AKN), (MJ), (LS), (CS).More details and instructions are provided at the beginning of the course.Assessment method:Each of the requested activities has a specific weight in the final evaluation:[60%]: 1) Written final exam at the end of the course in which students will have to reply to 4 in 80 minutes.[40%]: 2) Paper and final presentation at the end of the course.To approve the exam, attending students have to take 18/30 in each one of the two parts.NON-ATTENDING students are evaluated only on their performance in the Final Exam (100%). Non-attending students will have to reply to 6 questions out of 6 in 120 minutes.ATTENDING students are those who participate to the teamwork, i.e., by December, write a paper on a topic of their choice (from a list provided by the Professor) and present it in class using slides.Final mark goes from minimum 18 (D) points to 30 points (A). If the total evaluation is <18 (F) the preparation is not considered adequate and the student needs to retake the written test (only). In some cases, for excellent preparation, a student may get 30 points 'cum laude' (A+).

data.Contenuti: The objective of this course is to introduce the fundamental concepts at the basis of massive data management and analysis, including the main processing techniques dealing with data at massive scale and their implementation on distributed computational frameworks. The core notions of relational databases, as well as recent NoSQL solutions will be covered.
data.Testi: The lecture slides are based on the following textbook:Andreas Meier , Michael Kaufmann. "SQL & NoSQL Databases. Models, Languages, Consistency Options and Architectures for Big Data Management", Springer Vieweg Wiesbaden. Softcover ISBN 978-3-658-24548-1, eBook ISBN 978-3-658-24549-8.DOI https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-658-24549-8Additional material and references can be distributed during the lessons.After each classroom lesson the slides are published in the e-learning.
data.Obiettivi formativi: Knowledge and understandingKnowledge of the fundamentals of relational databases, such as keys, integrity and primary / foreign key constraints, as well as the SQL language for defining, manipulating and querying data, as well as NoSQL solutions for unstructured data.Applied knowledge and understandingUse the SQL language to create and query relational database structures, as well as understand and apply the principles of data organization in NoSQL systems. In particular, the student will be able to apply the core notions of data modeling in relational databases, to use the SQL language for creating and querying relational database structures, to apply the principles of data organization in NoSQL systems.Autonomy of judgmentThe student will be able to evaluate the circumstances in which the acquired tools and skills are applicable, to evaluate critically the results, to define practical policies. Communication skillsThe student will be able to use the keywords of databases and big data, to understand the description of a data storing/retrieving problem, to produce and discuss a technical report on a real case. Ability to learnThe student will be able to: (1) identify and frame a data management problem under a relational model; (2) identify the programming tools suitable for dealing with it; (3) autonomously search for innovative approaches and solutions.
data.Prerequisiti: Basic concepts on Computer Science, in particular Data representation and Boolean Algebra.
data.Metodi didattici: The educational objectives highlighted here are achieved through lectures, seminars, laboratory activities with the use of computers, individual and group projects, and exercises.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The exam is both written and oral. In the written part the student solves some short SQL exercises and answers questions about definitions and theoretical concepts. During the oral part, students are asked to discuss the answers of the written part with the teacher. Each test is evaluated on the basis of: - the relevance of the answer to the question - the correct syntax of the SQL language

data.Contenuti: L’insegnamento si occupa di fornire all* student* le principali teorie relative allo sviluppo e all’evoluzione delle crisi finanziarie. Il corso si propone inoltre di presentare le possibili risposte in termini di politiche monetarie e prudenziali.La prima parte del corso si focalliza sulla tipizzazione delle caratteristiche comuni a molte crisi finanziarie, facendo particolare riferimento alla grande depressione del 1929 e alla grande recessione del 2008. Nella seconda parte del corso vengono analizzati, e simulati mediante il software di calcolo R, alcuni dei modelli computazionali più importanti per lo studio delle bolle speculative e delle crisi finanziarie. La terza parte del corso si occupa delle politiche monetarie e prudenziali per arginare e prevenire le crisi finanziarie.

data.Obiettivi formativi: Conoscenza e capacità di comprensioneAlla conclusione del corso, l* student* avrà la capacità di individuare gli elementi tipici di una crisi finanziaria e di una bolla speculativa e delle possibile risposte che le istituzione pubbliche e/o sovranazionali possono intraprendere.Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensioneL* student* apprenderà inoltre ad impostare e simulare alcuni semplici modelli computazionali ad agenti eterogenei per studiare gli effetti delle crisi finanziarie.Autonomia di giudizioAl termine dell’insegnamento, l* student* dovrà aver acquisito la capacità di interpretare criticamente i principali fenomeni di crisi finanziaria, anche attraverso la simulazione di modelli, la raccolta dati e l'utilizzo di informazioni da fonti adeguate e attendibili.Abilità comunicativeL* student* dovrà essere in grado di comunicare a diversi interlocutori, in modo efficace e con un linguaggio appropriato, le proprie riflessioni sugli argomenti trattati.Capacità di apprendereL* student* dovrà aver maturato la capacità di intraprendere in modo il più possibile autonomo studi più complessi e approfonditi, attraverso il perfezionamento di un adeguato metodo di studio.
data.Prerequisiti: Sono richiesti una buona conoscenza della macroeconomia, della lingua inglese e competenze di base del software R.
data.Metodi didattici: Lezioni frontali e “flipped classrooms” con discussione in aula dei principali articoli di riferimento. Per la completa comprensione dei modelli, sono anche previste sessioni di coding e di simulazione mediante il software R. Per l’ottima fruibilità del corso, l* student* è invitat* a frequentare con costanza e a leggere gli articoli indicati nel syllabus prima di ogni lezione. Questo permetterà di trasformare alcune delle lezioni in dibattiti moderati dal docente.
data.Altro: Nessuna
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: Esame orale con progetto di approfondimento. L* student* (anche in gruppo) dovrà preparare un progetto su temi specifici e presentarlo in sede di esame. Si potrà scegliere tra un progetto in formato “literature review” ed un progetto in formato “estensione di un modello”. Maggiori dettagli verranno forniti durante le prime lezioni del corso.

data.Contenuti: The course consists of four components: (i) foundations; (ii) the economics of pollution control; (iii) international environmental problems & cooperation; (iv) project appraisal and evaluation.PART I deals with the foundations of environmental (and resource) economics. In particular, it outlines the fundamental characteristics of an economic approach to environmental analysis, discusses the economy-environment interdependence, and examines the ethical underpinnings of environmental economics. It ends with a comprehensive review of the theory of welfare economics, and provides the fundamental economic tools that will be used throughout the course.PART II covers what is usually thought to be “environmental economics”; that is, the analysis of pollution. We deal here with pollution targets and methods of attaining them (i.e., pollution control instruments). We are careful to pay proper attention to the relative strengths and weaknesses of alternative methods, especially in the presence of uncertainty. The analysis is supported by both theoretical arguments and empirical examples.Many environmental problems spill over national boundaries, and can only be successfully dealt with by means of international cooperation. This is the focus of PART III. A central feature of this component is our use of game theoretic concepts and tools to study the extent and evolution of international environmental cooperation. Insights from the theory are then used to analyze the success and challenges of cooperation over specific issues, with an emphasis on climate change.The last component (Part IV) is concerned with the principles and practice of project appraisal. We provide here an overview of commonly used evaluation methods, examine their theoretical underpinnings and provide examples of application. We conclude with a discussion of the insights that the field of behavioural economics brings to the analysis and evaluation of environmental problems.
data.Testi: Detailed reading lists will be provided to support each course component. The following textbooks will be particularly useful:• Perman, R., Y. Ma, J. McGilvray and M. Common, Natural Resource and Environmental Economics, Pearson Addison Wesley: Fourth Edition (2011).• Kolstad, C., Environmental Economics, New York: Oxford University Press, 2011. Second Edition.Where appropriate, chapters from these texts will be selected as core readings for the respective week of teaching. The above resources will be complemented with other reading material, including chapters from other books, journal articles and reports. The readings for each week of teaching will be made available on ESSE3.
data.Obiettivi formativi: This course seeks to develop a rigorous treatment of the theory of environmental economics and show how formal economic thinking can assist real world policymaking in areas such as climate change, air pollution control, water resource management at different levels of governance. At the end of the course, students will be able to demonstrate the following:- Thorough knowledge and understanding of the principles and conceptual foundations of environmental economics. - Ability to apply the tools of microeconomic analysis to the environment. - Command of the literature and ability to critically reflect on current debates.- Ability to apply the acquired knowledge to new problems and contexts and provide policy recommendations which are solidly grounded in environmental economics thinking.- Proficiency in the following transferrable skills: professional writing, through writing of essays; communication skills through class debates and break-out group exercises; problem solving and application of numeracy skills, through solving formal exercises and problem sets.
data.Prerequisiti: A solid background in economics is desirable.
data.Metodi didattici: Teaching is delivered through weekly lectures. Lectures are grounded in formal economic analysis and intended to: (i) guide students through the reading material, and (ii) provide a conceptual framework through which subsequently explore applications and examples. During the lectures, we will make use of formal problem sets, debates and break-out group exercises to help develop analytical skills and critical thinking.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: A 1.5 hrs unseen examination, consisting of multiple choice questions and open questions/exercises.

data.Contenuti: Nel corso saranno affrontati i seguenti argomenti: una sintetica analisi dei diversi prodotti di risparmio gestito; le modalità di costruzione e le conseguenti possibilità di replica di un benchmark; l’analisi delle determinanti della performance di un portafoglio di investimento; i limiti dell’asset allocation strategica basata sul modello media-varianza e le possibili soluzioni; la valutazione della performance; il ruolo degli investitori istituzionali nel sistema finanziario italiano; le politiche di gestione di portafogli istituzionali di tipo tradizionale; le politiche di diversificazione di portafoglio verso asset class alternative; il controllo del rischio nell'asset management.
data.Testi: I.Basile, M.D. Braga, P. Ferrari (a cura di); Asset management e investitori istituzionali. 3^ edizione; Pearson; 2024In aggiunta a ciò, saranno consegnate alcune esercitazioni volte a permettere l’acquisizione di una pratica operativa sui temi teorici affrontati in aula. Tali esercitazioni sono obbligatorie e concorreranno alla formazione della valutazione finale.
data.Obiettivi formativi: Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione: il corso si propone di fornire conoscenze specialistiche nell’ambito della gestione del risparmio e degli investitori istituzionali. In particolare sono analizzati: i prodotti del risparmio gestito, i benchmark, le fasi della gestione di portafoglio, l’asset allocation strategica, la valutazione della performance, gli investitori istituzionali, la gestione di portafoglio tradizionale e con l’inclusione di asset class alternative, il controllo del rischio.Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione applicate: lo studente dovrà essere in grado di esporre i temi trattati nel corso e di risolvere problematiche applicative legate alla gestione di portafogli.Autonomia di giudizio: il corso consente allo studente di affrontare in autonomia le problematiche della costruzione e gestione di portafogli, anche in relazione alle politiche degli investitori istituzionali.Abilità comunicative: lo studente sarà in grado di comunicare con operatori in campo finanziario, in modo efficace e con un linguaggio appropriato.Capacità di apprendere: lo studente dovrà aver maturato la capacità di analizzare la performance e i rischi degli investimenti in asset class tradizionali e alternative.
data.Prerequisiti: Si presuppongono acquisite le conoscenze di base del corso di Economia degli Intermediari Finanziari, di Economia del Mercato Mobiliare e di Matematica Finanziaria.
data.Metodi didattici: Lezioni frontali.E’ vivamente consigliata la frequenza alle lezioni, benché non vi sia alcuna forma di accertamento della presenza in aula.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: Gli esami sono svolti in forma scritta, attraverso due prove parziali oppure attraverso una prova unica finale. Le esercitazioni, sia individuali che di gruppo, concorreranno alla valutazione finale. L’ammissione alla seconda prova parziale è subordinata al superamento della prima prova parziale con un voto sufficiente. Il voto finale è rappresentato dalla media semplice dei voti riportati nelle due prove. Il superamento dell’esame esige che anche il voto della seconda prova parziale sia sufficiente. Gli esami scritti comprendono: esercizi, domande teoriche e domande a risposta multipla.In caso di svolgimento remoto, sia le prove parziali che l’esame completo sono tenuti in forma orale.

data.Obiettivi formativi: Presentare le istituzioni fondamentali del commercio elettronico e della protezione dei dati personali. Sviluppare negli studenti le competenze necessarie ad analizzare le questioni giuridiche e ad utilizzare gli strumenti giuridici idonei alla ricostruzione di risposte concrete nella composizione degli interessi giuridici ed economici coinvolti. Introdurre gli studenti all’interpretazione delle norme giuridiche nazionali ed internazionali in una prospettiva teleologica e sistematica.-Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione:Lo studente dovrà dimostrare di aver compreso le linee generali e le nozioni fondamentali dell’e-commerce, la problematica che esso comporta rispetto alla contrattazione tradizionale in presenza dei contraenti, con particolare riferimento alla normativa riguardante la tutela dei consumatori.-Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione:Lo studente dovrà dimostrare di conoscere i singoli istituti giuridici della materia, la loro collocazione concettuale nell'ambito del sistema e di avere una visione d’insieme sulla loro applicabilità nell’ambito del commercio on line.-Autonomia di giudizio:Lo studente dovrà dimostrare di aver acquisito la capacità di orientarsi attraverso i vari istituti nelle loro diverse applicazioni, anche in relazione all'esigenza di tutelare interessi differenti.-Abilità comunicative:Lo studente dovrà dimostrare di aver acquisito un adeguato livello nel linguaggio tecnico-giuridico e nell’argomentazione e la costruzione del ragionamento giuridico.-Capacità di apprendimento:Lo studente dovrà dimostrare una sufficiente capacità di apprendimento delle istituzioni generali dell’e-commerce, di sapere riconoscere le varie problematiche che il commercio attraverso internet pone ai consumatori e alle imprese e di sapersi orientare nella ricerca delle regole da applicare, con particolare riferimento nel settore della contrattazione di beni e servizi.

data.Contenuti: The course introduces the students to the basic principles that guide corporate managers and entrepreneurs in making their ordinary and extraordinary financing decisions in national and international companies. It also provides the analytical tools to operate in the financing and investing area.Topics covered include: financial analysis, cash flow estimation, time value of money, capital budgeting, the relationship between risk and return, cost of capital, capital structure decisions, company's valuation.
data.Testi: Vernimmen Pierre, Corporate finance. Theory and practice, 2022, 6th ed. John Wiley&Sons, ISBN 978-1-119-84162-3 - also available as an e-book on wiley.comIt is suggested to read the whole book. In any case the following chapters will not be used in the final test: 6, 7, 24, 25, 43, 51 and 52.
data.Obiettivi formativi: 1. Knowledge and understandingThe course introduces the students to the basic principles of financing and investing decisions, providing the analytical tools for assessing company’s financial situation and company's value.The aim is to provide students with a thorough understanding of techniques, theories and issues found in practical corporate finance situations.2. Applying knowledge and understandingThe objective of the course is to strengthen the knowledge of the principles of finance with the aim of providing students with the know-how required to operate as managers or entrepreneurs within an international company.At the end of the course the student will be able to:a. realize a financial analysis and determine the company’s financial situationb. conduct a capital budgeting analysisc. identify the future financial needs of the companyd. evaluate the financial debt sustainability and the company’s capital structuree. identify the company’s value according to the DCF model and the market3. Making judgementsAt the end of the course the student will be able to derive financial information from the company financial reporting and thus will be in a position to analyze and provide practical guidance to Senior Management4. Communication skillsThe student will be able to communicate with financial intermediaries and consultants in an effective way, leveraging on the industry language5. Learning skillsBy interacting with the professor, by solving exercises and working through case studies, the student will learn to analyze and evaluate the most often encountered financial problems in today’s companies. Emphasis is set on a proactive way to address problems.
data.Prerequisiti: No specific previous knowhow is mandatory except from the ones required by the Degree Program.
data.Metodi didattici: The course will alternate theoretical teaching – face to face lectures - and practical sessions on corporate cases and exercises to allow students to apply the concepts illustrated during classes.
data.Altro: The exam can be taken as an attending student or a non-attending student. Given that attendance of the course is not mandatory, it is at the student's discretion to declare himself or herself an attending or non-attending student.There is no limit in the academic year to take the exam as an attending student.The difference between the two examination modes lies in the fact that for attending students, the topics of the various lectures will be the subject of the examination. For non-attending students, the examination object will be the entire textbook with the exception of Chapters 6, 7, 23, 24, 51 and 52. It is also reccomended for attending student to read the suggested book.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: At the end of the course the exam will be a written test (exercises, open and multiple-choice questions) on the topics covered during the course. The test is closed book. A non-programmable calculator is allowed.There is a 30 point grading scale with highest result being 30/30 and pass result 18/30.Assessment: Final Mark

data.Contenuti: The course includes main notions and stages of decision making, unit and multi-criteria models, both under certainty and under uncertainty, and their use in applied problemsThe methodology will be applied to environmental issues, such as environmental regulation, water utility management, renewable energy management, and sustainable financeIn particular, the focus will be on• Introduction to Decision Problems• Introduction to Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis• Multi-Attribute Utility Theory• Analytic Hierarchy Process• Analytic Network Process• Data Envelopment Analysis• Decision-Making Under Uncertainty: Introductory Topics• Decision-Making Under Uncertainty: Monte Carlo SimulationThe applied topics will cover the study of• Environmental Regulation• Water Utility Management• Renewable Energy Management• Sustainable Finance

data.Obiettivi formativi: General tasksStudents will learn a disciplined, structured approach to rational decision-making without and with uncertaintySpecific tasks- Knowledge and understandingAfter the course, students will be able to--- account for fundamental aspects of Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) and Decision-Making Under Uncertainty (DMUU)--- apply basic principles of MCDA and DMUU in different cases--- describe the multi-dimensional and uncertain nature of environmental issues- Applying knowledge and understandingStudents, after this course, will learn a disciplined, structured approach to rational decision-making where environmental projects are judged according to appropriate sustainability criteria- Making judgementsAfter the course, students will learn to assess criteria on a qualitative and/or quantitative basis and to perform a comparative evaluation of potential competing projects- Communication skillsBy the end of the module, students should be able to understand and explain the basic concepts of multi-criteria optimization, to formulate real-world problems from management and environmental economics as multi-criteria optimization problems, to discuss different solution concepts, their advantages and their limitations in practice, to apply and justify several solution methods for multi-criteria optimization problems and discuss their drawbacks and their advantages- Learning skillsThe contents of the course are provided through various teaching methods. They are aimed not only at developing the ability of understanding and applying knowledge, with independent judgment and adequate communication skills, but also at increasing the knowledge on contents similar to those of teaching
data.Prerequisiti: There are no pre, post, and co-requisites to the study of Methods and Models for Environmental Sustainability
data.Metodi didattici: The weekly lectures of the course are grounded in formal economic analysis and are intended to guide students through the reading of materials and provide a conceptual framework for a subsequent exploration of applications and examplesDuring the lectures, use of formal problem sets, debates, and break-out group exercises will be made to help develop analytical skills and critical thinkingPart of the course will be developed with dedicated software
data.Altro: Computer usage: some homework assignments can be efficiently solved with a computerE-mail and webpage: homework assignments, design problems, solutions, review sessions, and exam prospectuses will be emailed and/or posted on the course webpage

data.Testi: Paul Krugman, Maurice Obstfeld, Marc Melitz; International Economics: Theory and Policy (11th edition, global edition); Pearson; 2018; 978-1-292-21487-0;Capitoli 1-12, first part of 22.There is the possibility of obtaining a free open access copy at https://www.academia.edu/45169893/International_Economics_Theory_and_Policy_Global_Edition_by_Paul_R_Krugman_Maurice_Obstfeld_Marc_J_Melitz The new edition (12th edition, 2022) of the same book is available at https://www.pearson.com/uk/educators/higher-education-educators/program/Krugman-International-Economics-Theory-and-Policy-Global-Edition-12th-Edition/PGM100003100497.html In this edition there are updated examples and case studies: i) the impacts of Brexit and COVID-19 (Chapter 7)ii) firms' global sourcing decisions and the new USMCA treaty (Chapter 8)iii) US-China trade tensions (Chapter 10)iv) the effects of the Trump trade war on global trade and the COVID-19 pandemic (Chapter 19)v) the Dec. 2020 EU-UK trade deal plus the prior withdrawal agreement and its implications for the Irish border (Chapter 21)vi) euro area policy innovations in response to COVID-19 (Chapter 21)We'll go through some of these new issues via bibliographic material supplied in the Comunità Didattica. Digital tools (optional):www.MyEconLab.comFurther readings:Few readings and other material will be distributed in class and on-line, via Moodle platform "Comunità didattica" International Economics (A.A. 2022), regarding special issues and papers related to International Trade and Policy program.
data.Obiettivi formativi: a) Knowledge and understanding (KN)The students will be able to elaborate complex theoretical concepts regarding international economics, such as e.g. the absolute advantage and the comparative advantage (who trades what with whom and why), and the terms of trade. They will learn to solve models where resource distribution and use determine the pattern of trade, or where the market structure determines intra-industry trade. They will be able to identify gains from trade, what kind of policies countries apply and their effect on good prices and society welfare, and why developing countries have a different perspective about trade policy. They will deal with many case studies at hand.b) Applying knowledge and understanding (AKN)The students face empirical problems as well, especially regarding the evaluation of correlations and relationships between international trade aggregates on specific relevant topics, such as international competition (relative wages and productivity), the Leontieff paradox (skill-content of US imports and technologically-advanced trading partners), the double-causality effect of the crises. In order to achieve this objective, students learn to manage on-line databases, searching for adequate data, posing a research question, developing a method to get results and answering with complete and convincing conclusions.c) Making judgements (MJ)The students learn to formulate theoretically and empirically based arguments about past and current events of international trade such as why countries exchange goods, services or assets, what is the role of WTO in setting rules and solving disputes, and why countries need such an institution. Moreover, they can explain why policymakers today engage into applying tariffs and subsidies, especially in crucial sectors of the economy, and whether this is beneficial to trading countries. They learn to make judgements about the benefits or drawbacks of free trade, protectionism, and other levels of economic integration.d) Communication skills (CS)The students are required to present a team project in a poster session, in order to deliver one’s own abilities in communicating international trade concepts to a mixed (experts and not) audience in English. Moreover, students will be asked to discuss in class their own solutions to three home assignments.e) Learning skills (LS)This course gives a set of learning instruments that include homework problems to solve individually, the possibility to identify a research question and implement academic writing skills on a teamwork structured project with a deadline, and to make use of algebraic and graphic techniques to answer specific questions regarding international economics issues.
data.Prerequisiti: Pre-requisites:Students must have a good knowledge of Principles of Micro and Macroeconomics (undergraduate level), General Mathematics and English language. Proficiency in English is useful but not required.
data.Metodi didattici: It is advisable, even if not obligatory, to attend each lecture, because the course requires students’ active learning.The teacher takes notice of whom is attending each lecture. Only a presence of 75% or more (at least 18 lectures) gives a student the status of "attending student".Only attending students (either on-site or on-line for specific cases) participate to active learning: homework, discussion and final poster session.THE REST OF THE STUDENTS WILL BE CONSIDERED NON-ATTENDING.Non-attending students are required to study the textbook, reading all the material uploaded on Moodle platform "Comunità Didattica" International Economics (A.A. 2023), and take the final test in the official dates of exam. Example of past tests or exercises will be available in the Comunità Didattica at the end of the course.Optionally, students might study over the digital tool www.MyEconLab.com to get acquainted with interactive graphics, questions, and all the material in the required chapters.AS FAR AS ATTENDING STUDENTS, their final evaluation of knowledge (KN), applied knowledge (AKN), making judgements (MJ), learning (LS) and communication skills (CS) about IE is based on three components:1) Students are required to solve INDIVIDUALLY home assignments and critically discuss the solution in class [testing for (AKN), (MJ)] with a maximum of three homework (valued 2 points each). Students allowed by the dean of the Department to connect at distance can discuss their homework over the MS Teams platform, sharing their screen.2) By December, students will prepare a POSTER on a topic of their choice (from a list of topics or papers provided by the teacher) and present it in a POSTER SESSION, to experiment COMMUNICATION techniques related to International Economics. THIS IS A TEAM WORK; the teacher will set each team and evaluate both the team work and each individual capacity/knowledge [testing for (AKN), (LS), (CS)].More details and instructions will be given at the beginning of the course.3) Final test. Students are required to answer theoretical open questions and solve for exercises [testing for (KN), (MJ), (LS)]. The test dates are officially set by the calendar of the Department.WARNING: IF THE EMERGENCY OF THE PANDEMIC WILL SHOW UP AGAIN DURING THE SEMESTER, BOTH THE POSTER SESSION AND FINAL LECTURES WILL BE GIVEN ON-LINE, AT DISTANCE, OVER THE MS TEAMS PLATFORM.
data.Altro: Students are expected to attend the lectures, to study the main textbook, reading the slides, to solve for home assignments, and go through suggested readings for in-depth analysis.RULES FOR NON ATTENDING STUDENTS OR THE LATE-COMERS:Slides will be distributed to facilitate comprehension of the subject via the Moodle platform Comunità Didattica International Economics (A.A. 2023).Office hours and email are available tools to contact the teacher.They MAY start a forum on Moodle platform Comunità Didattica IE to get answers from the Community of the other students and the teacher.They HAVE access to past exams on Moodle platform Comunità Didattica IE.They MUST take the final test (at official dates) to pass the exam.Their final grade is based on the final test only. The test is based on four questions, two of them are exercises and two are theoretical questions on the models.In exceptional, serious and rare cases, the teacher (at her discretion) might allow non attending students to take an oral exam after the written test.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: ATTENDING students' final evaluation of knowledge (KN), applied knowledge (AKN), making judgements (MJ), learning (LS) and communication skills (CS) about IE is based on three components:1) Each student solves INDIVIDUALLY home assignments (exercises or data analysis with graphs and tables) and briefly but critically discusses the solution in class [testing for (AKN), (MJ)] for a maximum of three homework.2) By December, students prepare a POSTER on a topic of their choice (from a list provided by the teacher) and present it in a POSTER SESSION, to experiment COMMUNICATION techniques related to International Economics. This is a TEAM work, and the teacher sets each team. An evaluation of the work is given to the team and to each individual student [testing for (AKN), (MJ), (LS), (CS)].More details and instructions are provided at the beginning of the course.3) Written Final Test. Each student answers two theoretical and two technical questions, solving for exercises, about international economics [testing for (KN), (AKN), (LS)].Assessment method:[Weight] of each requested activities in the final evaluation:[20%]: 1) Total Homework.[50%]: 2) Poster session active contribution and participation at the end of the course.[30%]: 3) Written final test at the end of the course (at official dates).A positive final grade goes from a minimum (Italian grade system) of 18 points (D, in the Anglo-Saxon grade system) to 30 points (A). If the total evaluation is less than 18 (F) the preparation is not considered adequate and the student needs to re-take the written test (only). In some cases, for excellent preparation, a student may get 30 points 'cum laude' (A+).NON-ATTENDING students are evaluated only [100%] on their performance in the Final Test, which is an extended version of the final test for attending students. The Italian grading system applies.
data.Programma esteso: Extended Program:1. Introduction to International Economics.What is International Economics about?The gains from trade.The pattern of trade.How much trade.The Balance of Payment.Exchange rate determination.International Policy coordination.The International Capital market.2. An overview of World Trade.Size matters! The Gravity Model.Impediments to trade: distance, barriers, borders.Has the world gotten smaller?What do we trade?3. Labor Productivity and Comparative Advantage: the Ricardian Model.We build a model to explain how trade takes place.Production functions and the resource constraint. Deriving the Production Possibility Frontier (PPF), the scale parameter and MRT in a country.Assumptions on labor input requirement and productivity in two countries.An absolute advantage explanation of the gains from trade.One-factor Ricardian model: assumptions, derivation and solution.Comparative advantage and pattern of trade.Case study: War of the Roses.Opportunity cost of producing and MRT.Formal definition of Comparative Advantage (CA).Specialization.4. Specific Factors and Income Distribution.The specific factors model.What is a specific factor?International trade in the specific factors model.Income distribution and the gains from trade.5. Resources and Trade: the Heckscher-Ohlin Model.Two-factors Heckscher-Ohlin Model.Factor endowment, Capital and Labor.Price of factors: returns to labor and capital.Preferences.Technology.Factor returns with free trade.Two resource constraints and derivation of the PPF.Numerical example.Substitutability in factor inputs and the concavity of the PPF.Isovalue line and optimal production.Relative Prices and the pattern of trade.The declining labor share.Empirical evidence of the HO model.6. The Standard Trade Model.A standard model of a Trading Economy.Production Possibilities and Relative Supply.Relative Prices and Demand.The Welfare effects of changes in the terms of trade.Determining relative prices.7. External Economies of Scale and the International Location of Production.Economies of scale and international trade.Economies of scale and the market structure.The theory of external economies.Interregional trade.8. Firms in the Global Economy: Export Decisions, Outsourcing, and Multinational Enterprises.The theory of imperfect competition.Monopolistic competition and trade.Intra-industry trade.Trade costs and export decisions.Dumping.Horizontal and vertical FDI.Trade-offs in FDI, outsourcing, offshoring.9. The Instruments of Trade Policy.Import tariffs, customs duties.Case study: Steel Industry in the US in 2001.Case study: EU trade policy.Export tariffs.Case study: Pakistan raw cotton tax in 1988.Type of tariff: ad valorem or specific tariff.When a small importing country imposes a tariff: graphical representation, equilibrium prices, welfare effects.When Two countries trading one product: imposition of a tariff, graphical representation, international equilibrium price, who trades with whom.Quotas and subsidies.10. The Political Economy of Trade Policy.The case for free trade.National welfare argument against free trade.Income distribution and trade policy.International negotiations and trade policy.the History of GATT.Case study: Banana Republic: trade dispute over bananas.Free Trade Areas: NAFTA.The degree of economic integration, regional integration in the world and free trade areas.Do agricultural subsidies hurt the third world?Other Trade policies: Government procurement, export credit subsidies, regulation.Summarizing the effect of alternative trade policies.11. Trade Policy in Developing Countries.Import-substituting industrialization.The infant industry argument.Case study: Mexico.Trade liberalization since 1985.India's boom.12. Controversies in Trade Policy.Technology and externalities.Imperfect competition and strategic trade policy.Globalization and low-wage labor.Globalization and the environment.22. Developing countries: Growth, Crisis, and Reform.Income, wealth, and growth in the World Economy.The Gap between Rich and Poor.Has the world income gap narrowed over time?The importance of developing countries for global growth.Structural features of developing countries.

data.Obiettivi formativi: KNOWLEDGE and UNDERSTANDING:At the end of the course, students must have developed the knowledge of a set of mathematical and financial tools that are necessary to the analysis of international business and economics.APPLYING KNOWLEDGE and UNDERSTANDING:At the end of the course, students must be able to apply the principal techniques of derivatives pricing; to apply theory to situations and cases in business and economics and forward arguments to justify or criticize aspects of business activity and macroeconomic modeling and to use standard software to model real situations.MAKING JUDGMENTS:At the end of the course, students must be able to create links among notions acquired during the course and to tackle financial and business problems through the use of logical and formal mathematical tools.COMMUNICATION SKILLS:At the end of the course, students must have the ability to communicate clearly and effectively the acquired knowledge.LEARNING SKILLS:At the end of the course, students must have developed good learning skills, which allow them to independently apply the knowledge acquired to the course of their studies.

data.Contenuti: La crescente complessità e discontinuità del sistema economico ha reso ancor più rilevante che in passato la capacità di prevedere l’avvicinarsi di una situazione di crisi e di intervenire in modo tempestivo al ﬁne di avviare un eﬃcace percorso di risanamento. La capacità di superare con successo la crisi dipende sia da interventi di tipo economico/aziendali sulla gestione sia dall’utilizzo di strumenti giuridici speciﬁcamente introdotti dal legislatore per agevolare il risanamento dell’impresa in crisi. In particolare il ritorno all’economicità dell’azienda dipende, anche, dalla “ﬁducia” che la stessa riesce ad acquisire dai principali stakeholders (creditori, banche, ﬁsco, ecc) mediante la condivisione di un eﬃcace “progetto di risanamento” nel quale indicare le cause e le ipotesi di soluzione della crisi, nonché le modalità con le quali tornare ad operare e creare valore per tutti gli interlocutori aziendali.
data.Testi: Testi di supporto. E.Giacosa - A.Mazzoleni, il progetto di risanamento dell’impresa in crisi, Giappichelli, Torino, 2012. E.Giacosa - A.Mazzoleni, I modelli di previsione delle insolvenze aziendali, Giappichelli, Milano 2018. Altro materiale di aggiornamento sarà reso disponibile on line
data.Obiettivi formativi: Diﬀondere la consapevolezza che la crisi rappresenti una fase ﬁsiologica della vita d’impresa di fronte alla quale l’approccio deve essere strutturato e professionale, nonché tempestivo. In particolare, esistono scelte gestionali e strumenti eﬃcaci per agevolare il risanamento dell’impresa in crisi che dovrebbero diventare patrimonio comune di tutti i soggetti che, a vario titolo, studiano o si occupano d’impresa. Obiettivo del corso è quello di approfondire le tematiche relative alla previsione della crisi d’impresa e le attività necessarie al suo risanamento. Viene analizzato, altresì, il funzionamento dei principali strumenti giuridici previsti dal legislatore italiano in tema di crisi e risanamento. Gli obiettivi del corso possono essere meglio articolati come segue: - Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione. Il corso permette di comprendere l’esistenza di una situazione di crisi aziendale oltre alle modalità con le quali avviare il percorso di risanamento sia attraverso interventi di natura economico aziendale sia attraverso l’utilizzo di appropriati strumenti di tipo giuridico. Vengono altresì approfondite le principali tecniche di previsione della crisi d’impresa atte ad avviare in modo tempestivo gli interventi di risanamento prima che la crisi si trasformi in insolvenza ed, inﬁne, in dissesto. Vengono altresì approfondite le modalità di con le quali l’impresa in crisi comunica ai suoi interlocutori la propria situazione. - Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione. Il corso stimola la capacità degli studenti di applicare quanto appreso in un documento organico nel quale evidenziare le cause della crisi ed il percorso di risanamento traducendo, altresì, gli interventi programmati in valori economici, patrimoniali e ﬁnanziari previsionali. Tale documento è comunemente noto come progetto o piano di risanamento e rappresenta lo strumento con il quale l’impresa comunica ai propri interlocutori la propria strategia di risanamento nonché la capacità di tornare a creare valore sostenibile. - Autonomia di giudizio. Il progetto di risanamento dell’impresa permette di sintetizzare ed organizzare in modo sistemico tutte le informazioni sia di natura storica sia di natura previsionale attraverso le quali si forma il giudizio in ordine alla capacità dell’impresa di risolvere la crisi e tornare ad operare secondo corretti criteri di economicità. Viene quindi stimolata la capacità di giudizio dello studente in ordine alle concrete possibilità dell’impresa di aﬀrontare con eﬃcacia il proprio percorso di risanamento. L’approccio critico e la capacità di giudizio viene altresì stimolata dalle testimonianze di esperti di risanamento aziendale previste durante il corso. - Abilità comunicative. Lo studente svilupperà le proprie abilità di comunicazione anche mediante la presentazione di un caso di studio rappresentato da un progetto di risanamento che verrà predisposto in gruppi ristretti dagli studenti frequentati e presentato al docente ed agli altri studenti. In questa sede oltre alla comprensione dei fenomeni verrà sviluppata la capacità di trasferire messaggi ﬁnalizzati a convincere l’interlocutore sulla bontà del risanamento in atto. - Capacità di apprendere. La capacità di apprendere dello studente verrà stimolata attraverso lezioni teoriche, testimonianze aziendali e lavori di gruppo discussi in aula. I contenuti teorici verranno trasferiti attraverso le lezioni d’aula mente le testimonianze di esperiti di risanamento contribuiranno a stimolare l’approccio critico e la capacità di giudizio degli studenti. La discussione dei casi in aula sarà ﬁnalizzata, anche, a sviluppare le abilità comunicative degli studenti.
data.Prerequisiti: Sono date per acquisite le conoscenze maturate nel corso di Economia Aziendale.
data.Metodi didattici: Il corso è articolato in un ciclo di lezioni teoriche e di discussione in aula di casi aziendali. Sono previste alcune testimonianze di esperti di crisi e risanamento su speciﬁci temi trattati in aula.

data.Contenuti: The course focuses on the key practice through which leading decision makers cope with different task-environments, by enhancing peer relations within and between international organizations. Specific attention is drawn to those open collaborative networks emerging from a bottom-up perspective that accounts for a socio-cognitive perspective. Each issue is addressed by upholding a continuous reference to the typical conceptual frameworks of complex organizations involved in international business relations. Emerging capabilities of transformational leadership are studied by comparing dynamics of various organizations: multinational, international, global and also transnational companies.
data.Testi: Textboook (for non attending students)*Goldstein J., Hazy, J. K., and Lichtenstein, B. B. (2010) Complexity and the Nexus of Leadership. Leveraging NonLinear Science to Create Ecologies of Innovation, Palgrave Macmillan, New YorkRecommended reading:*Kupers, R. (2001) What Organizational Leaders Should Know about the New Science of Complexity. Complexity, 6(1), pp. 14-19*Ulh-Bien, M., Marion, R. and McKelvey, B. (2007) Complexity Leadership Theory: Shifting Leadership from the Industrial Age to the Knowledge Era. The Leadership Quarterly, 18(4), pp. 298-318.*McKelvey, B. (2010) Complexity Leadership: The Secret of Jack Welch’s Success. Int. J. Complexity in Leadership and Management, 1(1), pp. 4-36.* Vidaillet, B. 2001. "Cognitive Processes and Decision Making in a Crisis Situation: A Case Study." In T. Lant and Z. Shapira (eds.), Organizational Cognition. Mahwah, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum, pp. 241-263.---------------------The articles will be available as pdf files in the online course materials..
data.Obiettivi formativi: The course aims to provide students the main relational and coordination skills that are typical of organizations operating on international markets. This shall be referred both to the case of firms concerned with direct activity of foreign assets and to others merely involved in indirect asset-driven activity. Such an approach is focused on several cognitive-relational capabilities that are required to face the variety of cultural contexts, diversity, internal/ external innovation, peer-to-peer relationships and face-to-face interactions. Knowledge and understanding: students shall be able to deal with the basic principles of organizational decision-making in dynamic and highly uncertain environments. The course will frame leadership through the understanding of the three fundamental spheres of socio-organizational behavior of international firms: cognitive, procedural and symbolic one.Applying knowledge and understanding: the student shall be able to effectively and logically explain the process that allows an organization to bring out an appropriate style of leadership with regard to the social and international economic context in which firms operate. Specific emphasis is placed on improving the provision of negotiating capabilities that leading decision-makers should achieve as active managers in international business relations.Making judgement:at the end of the course, the student is supposed to embrace the capability of critically evaluating the main empirical problems of coordination involved in complex organization choices. Data and indicators should be used in a way that facilitates the understanding of international business scenarios.Communication skills: the student shall be able to argue on two levels: the scientific one, with specific terminology appropriateness, and the disseminating one, with addressed towards explaining notions even to non-professionals people.Learning skills: the student shall benefit from the acquired theoretical and empirical knowledge so that he/she could face the recurrent issues dealing with leadership for international business firms.
data.Prerequisiti: None
data.Metodi didattici: The course will integrate theoretical issues with case-studies by classroom teaching. It could also include home/group works as well as students' presentations.
data.Altro: No additional information
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The final grade will be based on a written test with 12 multiple choice questions (2 grade-points each one, no penalties for wrong answers) and 2 open-ended questions (from 0 to 3 grade-points each one). In agreement with the teacher and during the course, attendants can perform home/group works on specific topics by writing shorts reports and presenting/discussing them in the class during the last lectures. In this case, the final evaluation will be based 50% on the home/group work (up till 15/30) and 50% (up to the remaining 15/30) on the written test (in this case reduced to 3 open-ended questions; 5 grade-points each one). The structure of the final test is the same for attending and non-attending students (12 multiple-choice questions + 2 open-ended questions), while the content is obviously different, i.e.: for attending students the syllabus consists of the topics covered in classroom (what is contained in the course slides published on moodle + what was explained in class) while for non-attending students the syllabus consists of the text "Complexity and the Nexus of Leadership: Leveraging Nonlinear Science to Create Ecologies of Innovation" (by Goldstein, J., Hazy, J., Lichtenstein, B.)
data.Programma esteso: The course on leadership in complex organizations focuses on: (i) the relationship between collective decisions, cognition and innovation; (ii) the importance of open collaboration networks within and between organizations; (iii) the challenge of cultural diversity and the knowledge of new approaches to human resource management. More in details, the course will focus on the basic elements of the theory of complex adaptive systems, examining the main implications on the following fields of study: selective attention processes addressed towards the task-environment; the mechanisms of interaction within heterogeneous decision-making groups; conditions enabling the emergence of leadership if compared to the top-down one; advanced techniques that are able to apply in practice what was provided at theoretical level (for instance, the oval mapping technique for generating collective cognitive maps)

data.Contenuti: Logistics concerns the production, transportation and stocking of materials and products; supply chain management studies the logistic problems of a company in relation with its suppliers and customers and aims at the global optimization of the overall system. The course includes an introduction to logistic problems and supply chain management and aims at an enhanced understanding of the following topics and related decision models: supply network design and planning, inventory management, demand forecasting, coordination in a supply chain. Particular attention is paid to the environmental impact and sustainability of logistics systems.
data.Testi: Textbook: Chopra, Meindl. Supply Chain Management (6th ed - Global), Prentice Hall, 2016, ISBN-13: 978-1292093567.Some notions and examples will be taken from Simchi-Levi, Kaminsky, Simchi-Levi. Designing and Managing the Supply Chain (3ed), McGraw-Hill, 2008, ISBN-13: 978-0073341521 and from Coyle, Langley, Novack, Gibson. Supply chain management: a logistics perspective (10th ed.), Cengage Learning, 2017, ISBN-13: 978-1305859975.
data.Obiettivi formativi: Knowledge and understanding: (a) understand the role and complexity of the supply chain; (b) understand the problems faced in inventory management, supply network design, supply network management, demand forecasting; (c) understand the role of quantitative models in logistics management; (d) understand the environmental impact of supply chain decisions.Applied knowledge and understanding: Skills, qualities and attributes: develop spreadsheet models concerning inventory management, network planning, aggregate planning, demand forecasting; interpret the results, and suggest solutions to support decisions.Autonomy of judgment: The student will be able to evaluate the areas in which the acquired tools are applicable, to use advanced quantitative methods and to evaluate critically the results, in order to define practical management policies. Communication skills: At the end of the training activity, the student will be able to understand and use the keywords of supply chain management, to understand the description of a complex logistic system, to produce a technical report on a real case. Ability to learn: At the end of the course, the student will be able to: (1) identify and frame a management problem in a logistic context, at either strategic, tactical or operational level, according to a scientific / technological approach; (2) identify the quantitative tools suitable for dealing with it; (3) autonomously search for innovative approaches and solutions.
data.Prerequisiti: Specific skills and / or previous knowledge other than those required for enrollment in the Master program are not required.
data.Metodi didattici: Lectures in the classroom and exercises in the computer lab. The lessons include discussion of the theoretical framework and tools, and development of decision models with numerical examples. The lab exercises focus on the development, implementation, and resolution of specific models.
data.Altro: The program and the exam are the same for attending students and non-attending students.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The exam consists of a written test and homework (optional). The written test contains four open questions and two numerical exercises, and it covers all parts of the program. Questions will include descriptive elements but also critical elements. A correct use of terminology and a clear and concise presentation that highlights the logical connections between the aspects considered is necessary for a positive evaluation of the answers. Exercises will have a level of difficulty not higher than the level of the examples carried out during the lessons and laboratory sessions and will be inspired by the examples and exercises of the textbook. Each question/exercise weighs 5 points, for a maximum of 30 points. During the lessons, optional individual tasks (homework) will be assigned, to be delivered by set dates. The tasks will consist in small cases and exercises. The delivered homework will be evaluated in the end of the teaching period, assigning at most 3 additional points. These points will remain valid until the end of the academic year.
data.Programma esteso: (1) An overview of logistics and supply chain management: the complexity of the supply network, objectives and uncertainties, cycle view and push-pull view. Supply chain drivers and metrics: the role of facilities, inventory, transportation, information, sourcing and pricing.(2) Inventory management: exploiting economies of scale (EOQ model, order aggregation, discount policies), facing uncertainty (safety stock, periodic vs. continuous replenishment, risk pooling).(3) Transportation: transportation modes and their characteristics, issues and trade-offs in transportation management, models for transportations optimization.(4) Designing the distribution network: factors influencing network design, a framework for network design decisions, models for supply network design.(5) Aggregate planning: problem definition, strategies, linear programming models; building a rough master plan schedule.(6) Sourcing and supplier selection: in-house/outsource decisions; multicriteria analysis for supplier selection.(7) Demand forecasting in a supply chain: components of forecasts and forecasting methods, time series forecasting methods.(8) Coordination in a supply chain: the value of information and the bullwhip effect, managerial levers to achieve coordination and strategic alliances.

data.Contenuti: This course provides an overview on the main issues related to transportation management. The course will introduce the main optimization problems encountered in this application area, along with the mathematical models and optimization techniques to support decision-makers working in the field. The course will also tackle the problems from a practical viewpoint, providing a more qualitative analysis also through the study of several case studies. A focus will be devoted to green logistics applications.
data.Testi: G. Ghiani, G. Laporte, R. Musmanno, Introduction to Logistics Systems Management: With Microsoft Excel and Python Examples, Wiley, 2022, ISBN 978-1-119-78939-0.The content of this course covers only Chapters 1 and 6. Slides and additional material will be uploaded to the elearning community of the course.
data.Obiettivi formativi: D1 - KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING. This course provides students with the tools to support a rational decision-making process within complex optimization problems related to transportation management. The student will learn qualitative, quantitative, and IT tools to support logistics managers in reducing the related costs while improving the service level provided. D2 - APPLYING KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING. This course will provide students with the ability to choose and apply the tools for decision-making through examples, exercises, and simplified case studies. The expected outcome is that the student will be able to apply such tools to solve problems in new or unfamiliar environments within broader and multidisciplinary contexts, whenever the ability to make complex decisions is needed.D3 - MAKING JUDGMENTS. At the end of this course, the student will be able to judge autonomously which tools for decision-making are the most suitable for tackling a problem arising in the area of transportation management. The expected outcome is that the student will be able to make judgments regarding the evaluation of the cost-effectiveness of different solutions, as well as on the impact of the solution applied by the manager on the logistics system. D4 - COMMUNICATION SKILLS. At the end of this course, the student will be able to understand, interpret, and explain the solutions produced, particularly in terms of the cost-effectiveness of different solutions, on the one hand, and the impact of the solution applied by the manager to the logistics system, on the other hand. The expected outcome is that the student will be able to communicate such pieces of information to specialist and non-specialist audiences clearly, unambiguously, and using the appropriate terminology.D5 - LEARNING SKILLS. The student will learn an innovative teaching method, based on Problem solving, where the ability to formulate optimization models will be acquired on the basis of simplified versions of real-life cases. Some of these models will be implemented in an optimization software. The corresponding solutions will be evaluated and communicated in terms of cost-effectiveness and impact on the logistics system. This method is a basis for having self-directed and autonomous learning skills.
data.Prerequisiti: Basic knowledge of calculus
data.Metodi didattici: The course is organized in theoretical lectures and tutorials provided in lab.
data.Altro: The participation in person to the classes is strongly recommended.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: There are no differences in terms of the examination procedure between attending and non-attending students.The exam is written and provided as an automated test (via Moodle). The assessment is composed of three parts: some exercises, a set of questions on the use of an optimization software, and a set of theoretical questions.The written exam is marked on a scale of 30, and the final mark is obtained by rounding to the nearest integer the sum of mark achieved in each single exercise or question of the exam.

data.Contenuti: The aim of the module is to give students the capabilities and the tools to identify, analyze and solve complex marketing problems. At the end of the module every student will be able to develop a marketing plan and marketing strategies.
