data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: L'esame prevede domande ed esercizi a risposta chiusa in quiz computerizzati (con penalizzazioni per le risposte errate), e, se in presenza, un esercizio scritto.  Per i soli iscritti al primo anno di corso è possibile sostenere due prove intermedie (la prima a circa metà del corso, la seconda in coincidenza con il primo appello d'esame). Il voto finale è determinato dalla media aritmetica delle due prove. Condizione necessaria (ma non sufficiente) per passare l’esame strutturato su due prove intermedie e’ di ottenere un punteggio superiore a 16/30 in entrambe le prove. Data questa condizione, la media aritmetica delle due prove intermedie deve essere maggiore o uguale a 18/30 per passare l’esame.

data.Contenuti: The course includes two modules, ‘Decision theory and multi-criteria analysis’ and 'Optimization methods in business analytics'. Please, refer to the two modules for details.
data.Testi: The course includes two modules, ‘Decision theory and multi-criteria analysis’ and 'Optimization methods in business analytics'. Please, refer to the two modules for details.
data.Obiettivi formativi: Knowledge and understandingAt the end of the course the student will have acquired theoretical and practical tools for modeling and solving complex optimization problems that arise in management of companies, institutions and public administrations, with particular attention to linear, integer and multi-criteria optimization models.Applied knowledge and understandingAt the end of the course, the student will have acquired the ability: (1) to use mathematical modeling to formulate complex decision problems; (2) to treat Multi-Criteria Decision Making Problems; (3) to implement and solve optimization models and to test their results over a complete set of scenarios.Autonomy of judgmentThe student will be able to evaluate the impact of the proposed solutions in the application contextCommunication skillsStudents who successfully complete this course will be able to evaluate approaches to decision making and explain the strengths and weaknesses of approaches; to produce a complete report on a real case including problem description, modeling approach, solution methods, results and practical insights.Ability to learnAt the end of the course, the student will have acquired the ability:(1) to apply the mathematical-modeling skills acquired to improve the products and services offered by companies, institutions, and public administrations;(2) to develop and implement mathematical optimization models identifying the quantitative and software tools suitable for dealing with them;(3) to make decisions that account for uncertainty and an individual’s risk attitude;(4) to create an objectives hierarchy to trade off among objectives in a multi-criteria decision problem;(5) to analyze and interpret the results of quantitative analysis from a managerial perspective, to take decisions based on the results of the mathematical models.

data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: Knowledge and skills are achieved and verified in the following compulsory training activities:- Decision theory and multi-criteria analysis;- Optimization methods in business analytics.The grade of the course will be given by the average of the grades of the two modules, rounded up. Both modules must have sufficient marks (mark greater or equal to 18/30). Each module will be evaluated through (1) assignments/projects and (2) a written exam. The written exam comprises two separate parts, one for each module. The two parts can be undergone separately. Honors are given to students that score at least 31 points out of 30 in the final mark of each module.Marks of each module will remain valid until March 2026.

data.Contenuti: L'analisi delle reti sociali (SNA) è una metodologia di ricerca che si concentra sulla struttura delle relazioni tra attori (o entità sociali) come individui, organizzazioni e comunità. Le tecniche di SNA sono ampiamente utilizzate nelle scienze sociali, politiche e comportamentali, nonché in economia, finanza, geografia e ingegneria. Inoltre, negli ultimi decenni gli studi di SNA sono diventati ancora più centrali, a causa della crescita delle forme organizzative basate su paradigmi di rete e per l'aumento della connettività globale. Con queste premesse, il Laboratorio fornirà le basi della SNA sia dal punto di vista teorico che pratico.

data.Obiettivi formativi: 1) Conoscenza e comprensioneIn primo luogo, il corso si propone di fornire, con un approccio prevalentemente interdisciplinare, un quadro concettuale che spieghi come la SNA possa affrontare questioni rilevanti nella ricerca sociale. In secondo luogo, le lezioni introdurranno al linguaggio tecnico di base della SNA. Terzo, il corso fornirà conoscenze sui principali progetti di ricerca archetipici basati sulla metodologia SNA. Quarto, le lezioni indicheranno come rendere operative le tecniche di dedicate alle variabili relazionali. Infine, verranno spiegati i principali meccanismi teorici alla base della formazione delle reti sociali, con particolare attenzione a: analisi delle reti organizzative (ONA), reti di conoscenza, reti di attività e reti di risorse.2) Applicare conoscenza e comprensioneCi si attende che gli studenti comprendano: come funzionano i principali software SNA (es. Gephi, NodeXL, Ucinet e Pnet); come utilizzare gli indici SNA più comuni; come impostare una ricerca empirica basata su SNA e come acquisire familiarità con le principali tecniche basate su procedure di mappatura cognitiva (orientate sia al confronto di mappe individuali sia alla costruzione di mappe collettive) e strumenti di teoria dei grafi per reti semantiche (anche in insiemi fuzzy e anche partendo da fonti testuali utilizzando software come WORDij o pacchetto R come Quanteda).3) Formulare giudiziAl termine del corso, ci si attende che gli studenti sviluppino una capacità analitica e autonoma di interpretare le questioni relative alla SNA, collegando argomenti interdisciplinari e fonti informative eterogenee.4) Abilità comunicativeCi si attende che gli studenti sviluppino capacità che permettano loro di comunicare efficacemente con i vari interlocutori, e confrontarsi sugli argomenti del corso con i colleghi, il docente e qualsiasi persona coinvolta nell'attività formativa. Fondamentale, in tal senso, sarà la capacità di applicare nozioni teoriche a contesti non familiari con una prospettiva interdisciplinare.5) Capacità di apprendimentoCi si attende che gli studenti sviluppino un metodo di studio efficace, che consenta loro di elaborare autonomamente questioni complesse e interdisciplinari.

data.Contenuti: L’insegnamento approfondisce l’economia aziendale come scienza che studia l’azienda in quanto fenomeno economico funzionale al soddisfacimento dei bisogni umani anche con riferimento alle opportunità offerte dalo sviluppo tecnologico. L’insegnamento ha lo scopo di fornire le conoscenze di base necessarie per comprendere: le condizioni di esistenza e le logiche di funzionamento delle aziende, secondo un’ottica sistemica e di sviluppo sostenibile; le metodologie e gli strumenti a disposizione dei soggetti preposti al governo ed al controllo delle aziende. L’insegnamento introduce, secondo un’ottica unitaria e sistemica, le diverse tipologie di aziende per approfondire, poi, le aree che contraddistinguono le organizzazioni aziendali nelle loro diverse fattispecie. Nello specifico, l’insegnamento sviluppa i seguenti argomenti: - L'Economia d'azienda: oggetto e principi generali; - La specializzazione economica; - I soggetti d'azienda e le finalità istituzionali; - L'approccio sistemico all'economia d'azienda; - L'azienda come sistema sociale; - I rapporti azienda / ambiente e le relazioni economiche tra aziende; - La struttura aziendale; - L'assetto istituzionale; - L'organismo personale e l'assetto organizzativo; - - Lo scambio, i mercati, i settori; struttura organizzativa e sistemi operativi; - La gestione; I sistemi di pianificazione, programmazione e controllo; - La strategia aziendale; - Internazionalizzazione e globalizzazione; - La responsabilità sociale di impresa; - Leadership e managerialità.

data.Obiettivi formativi: L’obiettivo dell’insegnamento consiste nel fornire solide conoscenze di base per comprendere i principi generali di funzionamento e di gestione aziendale caratterizzanti le differenti tipologie di aziende ed i differenti contesti. Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione. L’insegnamento si propone di fornire agli studenti le nozioni ed i principi fondamentali dell’economia aziendale, intesa come scienza sociale, ossia la conoscenza delle diverse tipologie di aziende, del loro funzionamento, dei principali stakeholder, del contesto di operatività aziendale. L’approccio utilizzato si basa su: l'unitarietà dei fenomeni aziendali (di gestione, di organizzazione, di rilevazione), la centralità delle persone, il rispetto delle condizioni di economicità, il progresso economico come strumento per il progresso civile e sociale, le relazioni con gli stakeholder interni ed esterni.Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione applicate. L’insegnamento intende far acquisire agli studenti la capacità di capire e sostenere con argomentazioni adeguate le principali tematiche economico-aziendali anche attraverso la raccolta di dati ed informazioni adeguati ed attendibili.Autonomia di giudizio: lo studente dovrà maturare un’adeguata autonomia di giudizio intesa come capacità di analizzare ed interpretare criticamente le principali dinamiche caratterizzanti le diverse tipologie di azienda.Abilità comunicative. L’insegnamento si propone di far acquisire un linguaggio appropriato per esprimere in modo adeguato le proprie riflessioni su argomenti di carattere aziendalistico.Capacità di apprendere: l’insegnamento intende stimolare la capacità di apprendimento autonomo finalizzato alla comprensione ed all’approfondimento di tematiche e fenomeni attuali relativi alla materia studiata.

data.Contenuti: In this course students will learn about a set of ideas and models helpful in understanding economies in which data are important inputs in the production process and inform firms' strategic choices. After a discussion of the specificities of information as an economic good, we will discuss the role of information and data as fundamental inputs in the process of economic growth. Theoretical and measurement issues will be addressed. We will then focus on the strategic use of data in competition between firms. A special attention will be devoted to data-brokers, platforms that collect data from consumers and sell them to third parties. Finally, we will discuss issues and cases of regulation and antitrust policies in digital markets.
data.Testi: C. Chamley (2003), Rational Herds, Cambridge University Press.P. Belleflamme and M. Peitz (2015) Industrial Organization, Cambridge University Press, selected chapters.Additional readings will be available of the course website
data.Obiettivi formativi: Knowledge and UnderstandingThis is a course in economic theory. We will discuss models on individual and social behavior based on the standard tools of microeconomic and macroeconomic theory, applied to economies in which information and data are essential elements. Applying knowledge and understandingThe hope is that working through the logic and basic properties of these models will help the students in understanding some aspects of our economic environment. In particular, the role that knowledge and data play in the process of economic growth, in shaping strategic competition between firms, in the design of taxation and regulation of firms.Making judgementsEffort will be made in linking the lessons learned from the analysis of abstract models to real world phenomena, so as to inform judgement. This should be helpful when making decisions in private and public organizations.Communication skillsStudents will be required to present arguments in a clear format both in the written exams and in the oral presentationsAbility to learnBeside understanding the logic and properties of the models, the students will be required to solve simple numerical exercises. They will also be asked to read some research papers and prepare a set of presentation slides. More generally, the emphasis will be on the ability to use simple abstract models to interpret a complex reality.

data.Contenuti: The main aim of this course is to provide students with an overview of some important topics in supervised and unsupervised statistical learning techniques. These will be applied in the framework of complex data sets in real-world and web-based business statistics. The course will be organized in a main theoretical part on machine learning, made up of six main units: (i) Introduction and overview; (ii) Tree-based methods; (iii) SVM; (iv) Unsupervised learning; (v) Survival analysis; (vi) Multiple testing. The R software will be adopted for applications throughout the course. For some insights and demonstrations in Python will be given.
data.Testi: Selected chapters from:• James G, Witten D, Hastie T, Tibshirani R. An introduction to statistical learning. New York: Springer, 2023Other useful readings:• Lindholm, A., N. Wahlstrom, F. Lindsten, and T. B. Schon (2022). Machine Learning - A First Course for Engineers and Scientists. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.• Rogers, S. and M. Girolami (2016). A first course in machine learning. New York: Chapman and Hall/CRC• Hastie T. et al. (2009). The elements of statistical learning. New York: Springer• Azzalini, A., Scarpa (2012). Data analysis and data mining: An introduction. Oxford: Oxford University Press
data.Obiettivi formativi: The formative goals are consistent with those of the Master in “Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management”. At the end of the course, students will gain skills in the following domains: (i) Knowledge and understanding: understand the main techniques of supervised and unsupervised machine learning presented in the course; proper implementation of these techniques through the software; developing the ability of interpreting and commenting an output(ii) Applying knowledge and understanding: apply these techniques to problems that are well grounded in a business context, in order to extract proper information from data, and translating knowledge into business decisions(iii) Making judgements: use appropriate machine learning methods and understand how to interpret results and the output of statistical software. The course also aims to improve students’ critical skills through the discussion of some contemporary issues in learning, like deep learning and problems related to the super learner(iv) Communication skills: draft report of analyses in plain written English; communicate acquired knowledge to experts and non-experts, also by means of advanced visualization analytic tools(v) Learning skills: students will augment their learning skills using a mixture of resources and tools made available during the course like books, online materials, scripts, demos. They will exercise themselves in integrating different sources of information, interpreting them critically and discovering new sources of knowledge
data.Prerequisiti: Fundamentals of descriptive and inferential statistics, basic to intermediate knowledge of the R software. Knowing other software for statistical computing or data analysis (e.g. SAS, Stata) is an advantage, but not required
data.Metodi didattici: Classes will be composed of different activities, including lessons, hands-on (R lab), group discussions, intervention of external experts and testimonials
data.Altro: If possible, students should bring their own laptops with R and RStudio (or another editor) already installed
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The assessment will be based on a comprehensive written examination (computer-based) made up of open questions (theory) and theoretical/practical exercises on all units of the course. This will also include the reproduction of some R code/function. This is not an open book examination, but selected code sources will be provided by the instructor and will be directly accessible in the examination room.
data.Programma esteso: (i) Introduction to machine learning and algorithms; (ii) Tree-based methods, classification trees, bagging and random forests, boosting, BART, application in R; (iii) Optimal separating hyperplanes, support vector classifier, feature expansion and SVM, comparison with logistic regression, SVMs in R (iv) Unsupervised learning: PCA and higher-component PCA, K-means clustering, hierarchical clustering, matrix completion, unsupervised learning in R; (v) introduction to survival data and censoring, proportional hazard models, estimation of Cox model and model assessment, examples in R; (vi) introduction to hypothesis testing, multiple testing and family-wise error rate, Bonferroni’s and Holm’s methods to control FWER, False discovery rate and Benjamini-Hochberg method, resampling approaches, multiple testing in R. The R software will be adopted for applications throughout the course. On some parts, applications in Python may be shown and discussed with the students.

data.Contenuti: The course illustrates the identification strategies for the quantitative evaluation of causal effects in economics and management using experimental, quasi-experimental and observational data. The course introduces students to the methodological and applicative problems of the randomized control trials, the quasi-experimental / natural experiment’s approach; the statistical matching methods, the difference-in-difference and regression discontinuity techniques, and the presence of heterogeneous treatment effects. The emphasis is on the practical implementation of each approach, at the end of the course students will be able to critically understand the application of these tools in the recent empirical economic literature and to apply these approaches to design their own impact evaluation.
data.Testi: Joshua D. Angrist and Jörn-Steffen Pischke, 2009 Mostly Harmless Econometrics: An Empiricist's Companion, Princeton University Press. Gábor Békés and Gábor Kézdi, 2021 Data Analysis for Business, Economics, and Policy, Cambridge University Press.Course material will be made available on the e-learning
data.Obiettivi formativi: The educational aims of the course are consistent with those of master degree in “Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management” as it provides the knowledge and the abilities to quantitatively assess the causal effects of economic, social and business policies. More in details:KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDINGThe students will learn how to identify the causal effects in economics and management using experimental, quasi-experimental and observational data. They will be introduced to the methodological and applicative problems of the randomized control trials, the quasi-experimental / natural experiment’s approach; the statistical matching methods, the difference-in-difference and regression discontinuity techniques, and the presence of heterogeneous treatment effects.ABILITY TO APPLY KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDINGLectures and classes focus on the practical implementation of each approach, and students are supported in the preparation of a project work on real data. Thus, at the end of the course students will be able to critically understand and apply the alternative evaluation strategies in a real context.AUTONOMY OF JUDGMENTLectures and classes stress strengths and weaknesses of the alternative evaluation approaches and data sources. In their project work, students are guided in the discussion of pros and cons of their methodological and data choices. Thus, at the end of the course students will be able to independently judge which evaluation strategies to apply in different cases.COMMUNICATION SKILLSLectures and classes show alternative ways to present assumptions and results to professional and general publics. In their project work, students are supported in the choice of the most effective tools for communicating among peers and to a general public.ABILITY TO LEARNThe course provides the necessary notions, the ability to apply them and the autonomy of judgment necessary to further improve the knowledge of more more advanced causal inference techinques and evualuation approaches and to critically understand the application of these tools in the recent empirical literature.
data.Prerequisiti: Students should know the principles of statistical inference, ordinary least squares and maximum likelihood estimates for probit/logit models
data.Metodi didattici: The teaching methods that will be applied are: frontal lessons; guided case studies;and project works.All students will be required to participate actively, each student can face the practical phases individually or in groups of up to four people. The use of a personal computer is incentivized.
data.Altro: All the students presenting the assigned project work in class by the end of the teaching period will be considered as attending students.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The learning assessment is made of two parts:Written exam. This is an open book exam, that is, students can have access to the textbook and notes of the course. There are three exercises, and students are asked to use estimation results, to interpret and use them to answer the questions. Project work. A simple research task is agreed with the students. Students will be required to find the suitable data for the research question, choose the appropriate techinques and write the necessary code. Attending students present their results in a 20-minute seminar in front of the class; non-attending students write a 20-page report to be discussed in an oral exam during the exam sessions. Code and datasets are due at least two days before the discussion of the results. The assessment of the project will take into account the ability to related the work done to the contents of the course, the knowledge of the techniques and the ad hoc code implemented by the students. The project work can be done by single students or in small groups of up to 4 students.The overall final marks is the weighted average of the marks of the two parts, where the weight of the written exam (project work) is 33% (67%) for the attending students and 50% (50%) for the non attending ones. Please notice that the project work compulsory and it is required also to students who do not attend classes.
data.Programma esteso: For each topic, references to the textbooks are provided (MHE: Mostly Harmless Econometrics; DABEP: Data Analysis for Business, Economics, and Policy)• Introduction: The experimental ideal, randomized control trials, the quasi-experimental approach and the observational studies. (MHE 1 & 2 + DABEP 1)• Regression, causality and matching methods (MHE 3 + DABEP 20 & 21)• Instrumental variables estimators (MHE 4)• Panel data, fixed effects and diff-in-diff analysis (MHE 5 + DABEP 22& 23 & 24)• Regression discontinuity designs (MHE 6)• Quantile treatment effects (MHE 7)

data.Contenuti: Main methods and models of statistical learning for modeling and understanding complex datasets, with a focus on supervised learning, with regression and classification methods. Contents include extensions of linear regression model, polynomial regression, logistic regression, and linear discriminant analysis; models for categorical data; resampling methods (cross-validation and bootstrap), linear model selection and regularization methods (subset selection, shrinkage methods, dimension reduction methods); nonlinear models, splines and generalized additive models. Computing is done in R, with integration of data analysis software that utilizes the R environment for statistical computing, through tutorial sessions and homework assignments. Case studies and applications focus on digital economy and management.

data.Obiettivi formativi: The educational objectives are consistent with those characterizing the degree program in “Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management” in which the course is inserted. The course is concerned with the development, use and discussion of the main statistical methods of models of statistical learning useful for the analysis of complex data, to develop evidence-based answers to relevant questions and then give a valid support to strategic decisions in the fields of economics, marketing, management control, business intelligence and social sciences.Case studies and applications are proposed in socioeconomics and management fields, with the final aim of learning how to react to challenges of big data and data-driven economy. Using real cases and applications, the course aims at providing operational and practical guidance to data science, useful to those who, in various corporate functions as well as in public institutions, are involved in collecting, analyzing, processing and evaluating qualitative and quantitative information related to socioeconomic and company data. In detail, students will gain the following skills:1) Knowledge and understanding: by means of a gradual learning process, linking the contents of this course with the educational objectives of the cycle degree program in which the course is inserted, students will acquire the methodological and applied knowledge about the main concepts of statistical learning and will be able to apply such knowledge by means of appropriate software.2) Applying knowledge and understanding: students will be able to implement statistical regression and classification models in order to extract proper information from data, useful to analyse real phenomena in several fields of economics and management, and to understand their most important aspects.3) Making judgements: students who successfully complete this course will be able to select the most appropriate statistical models, apply sound statistical methods, perform the analyses using statistical software, and organize results in order to draw conclusions and decide in uncertain situations, like in specific economic and business situations.4) Communication skills: students who successfully complete this course will be able to communicate, to experts and non-experts, data information and evaluations, also with the help of outputs from specific software and data visualization devices.5) Learning skills: the course is aimed to provide the methodological and applied knowledge of statistical learning, necessary to address subsequent studies, in particular the advanced courses in mathematics, statistics, computer science, the quantitative aspects of economics courses, the applied projects in laboratories and internships, the empirical analyses in the final thesis.
data.Prerequisiti: Descriptive and inferential statistics, basic knowledge of R programming.
data.Metodi didattici: Lessons and practicals with use of computer
data.Altro: If the computer lab cannot be used, students are required to bring their own laptops
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The exam covers all the topics in the Program and consists of two parts:(1) an online test on the Moodle e-learning platform including one open-ended and 5 closed-ended questions concerning theoretical topics and/or short applications of the studied methods; the overall grade of this test amounts to 16 maximum (6 for the open-ended question and 2 for each of the closed-ended questions);(2) a poster exam, consisting in a 5-minute presentation of a poster showing the results of a group project of data analysis using R, followed by an individual oral exam. In detail, a group of students prepare the project, the poster and its presentation. Students are graded on the content, organization and design of the poster itself, the oral presentation of the poster and the ability to answer questions on the poster. The grading of the poster exam occurs in two parts: the group grade (max 8) and an individual grade (max 8 points); the latter is based on a brief individual oral examination administered to each student in the poster group. Although students are permitted to “tag-team” the presentation, it is recommendable that each group chooses one person to be responsible for the presentation.Only at the teacher’s discretion, the poster exam can exceptionally be replaced by a computer-based test, carried out in the computer lab, requiring the analysis of one or more data sets using R and the interpretation of the obtained results. Students can carry out this test with the help of the course material.Final Evaluation: The two parts of the exam (online test and poster exam) are each worth 50% of the total score. The final grade is obtained as the sum of the two grades in the two parts. The exam is passed if the final grade is greater than or equal to 18. It will be given a final grade of 30/30 cum laude to the students who achieve a final score equal to 32.There are no differences between attending and non-attending students. The online test is aimed at verifying skill 1 (Knowledge and understanding).The poster exam (or the computer-based test) allows to verify skills 2, 3 and 4 (Applying knowledge and understanding, Making judgements, Communication skills).The skill concerned with autonomous study (5, Learning skills) is indirectly verified, because passing the exam is also made possible by the autonomous execution of exercises suggested by the teacher for homework.

data.Contenuti: The course aims at providing technical skills about coding/scripting aspects for data analysis. On one side, students will learn how to approach problems according to an algorithmic view. Students will learn some techniques for problem solving and how to use a programming language to provide a sound and formal description of a designed problem solution. On the other side, they will learn programming skill in Python and R, giving the basic concepts of algorithms with reference to the use of the Python language (syntax, data structures, data import / export in Python, data visualization in Python) and its applications in data science and analytics.
data.Testi: - Think Python How to Think Like a Computer Scientist - Allen Downey- Python Machine Learning. Unlock deeper insights into machine learning with thisvital guide to cutting-edge predictive analytics - Sebastian Raschka
data.Obiettivi formativi: Knowledge and understandingKnowledge of problem-solving techniques to address algorithmic problems. Knowledge of the Python programming language and of the R framework, with reference to the essential notions on data structures and control structures of both Python and R.Applied knowledge and understandingAnalyze problems and design formal algorithmic solutions; translate algorithmic solutions into computer programs; use Python and R libraries and functions for data analysis; interpret the obtained results.Autonomy of judgmentThe student will be able to evaluate the circumstances in which the acquired tools and skills are applicable, to evaluate critically the results, to define practical policies. Communication skillsThe student will be able to use the keywords of coding, to understand the description of a data processing problem, to produce and discuss a technical report on a real case. Ability to learnThe student will be able to: (1) identify and frame a data processing and decision problem in an algorithmic view; (2) identify the programming tools suitable for dealing with it; (3) autonomously search for innovative approaches and solutions.
data.Prerequisiti: Basic Information Technology and Spreadsheets
data.Metodi didattici: The educational objectives highlighted here are achieved through lectures, seminars, laboratory activities with the use of computers, individual and group projects, and exercises
data.Altro: The exam is a written test, divided as follows:The programming exercise consists in writing a program in python language.Three open theory questions on Python and Machine LearningThe exam lasts two hours and will take place face to face.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The written exam is organized in two parts.The first part of the exam is related to the assessment of skills, by writing a program in Python.The second part concerns a set of questions that aim to verify the student's knowledge of the various topics of the course and the specific technical terminology.

data.Contenuti: The course is taught by Dr. Giancarlo Turati, CEO at Fasternet s.r.l and President of innexHUB.Cybersecurity will be introduced from an IT perspective. Contents will include an introduction to cybersecurity and online threats, an up-to-date view of the latest developments of cybersecurity in data and system management, definition of threats to computer systems and the discussion of the possible countermeasures. data.Contenuti: L'obiettivo di questo corso è quello di introdurre i concetti fondamentali alla base della gestione e analisi dei dati, comprese le principali tecniche per l'elaborazione di dati in grandi volumi e la loro implementazione in framework di elaborazione distribuita. Le nozioni chiave di database relazionali, così come le recenti soluzioni NoSQL, saranno trattate durante il corso.
data.Testi: - P. Atzeni, S. Ceri, S. Paraboschi, R. Torlone, Basi di Dati: Modelli e linguaggi di interrogazione McGraw-Hill Italia, 2013- S. Foresti, E. Pedrini, S. De Capitani Di Vimercati, Eserciziario di basi di dati, Pitagora editrice, 2006
data.Obiettivi formativi: Acquisizione di conoscenza sui concetti fondamentaliAcquisizione di conoscenza sui fondamenti dei database relazionali, quali chiavi primarie, vincoli di integrità, di chiave primaria e di chiave esterna, linguaggio SQL per definire, manipolare e interrogare basi di dati, soluzioni NoSQL per la gestione di dati destrutturati e semi-strutturati (XML, JSON).Applicazione dei concetti acquisitiApplicazione dei principi di modellazione di database relazionali e NoSQL. Uso del linguaggio SQL per creare e interrogare database relazionali. Applicazione dei principi per l'organizzazione di dati in sistemi NoSQL. Autonomia di giudizioLo studente sarà in grado di valutare le circostanze in cui applicare correttamente gli strumenti e le conoscenze acquisite nel corso, di valutare criticamente i risultati, di definire strategie di gestione dei dati. Capacità di esposizioneLo studente sarà in grado di utilizzare correttamente le parole chiave relative alle basi di dati e ai big data, comprendendo la descrizione di problemi di salvataggio/interrogazione di dati, per produrre e valutare documenti tecnici in casi reali.Capacità di apprendimentoLo studente sarà in grado di: (1) identificare e circoscrivere problemi di gestione dei dati utilizzando il modello relazionale; (2) identificare gli strumenti adatti per affrontare tali problemi; (3) trovare in autonomia approcci e soluzioni innovativi.
data.Prerequisiti: Basic programming
data.Metodi didattici: Gli obiettivi educativi messi in evidenza in questo contesto saranno raggiunti tramite lezioni e attività di laboratorio, utilizzando computer, sviluppando progetti individuali e di gruppo, svolgendo esercizi.
data.Altro: Durante il corso verranno forniti riferimenti a materiale liberamente disponibile in rete per approfondire i concetti trasmessi a lezione.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: Allo studente verrà chiesto di modellare una base di dati utilizzando schemi concettuali, di trasformare il modello concettuale in modello logico (e.g., relazionale), di interrogare la base dati così progettata utilizzando i principi dell'algebra relazionale e il linguaggio SQL. L'esame consisterà in una prova scritta.

data.Contenuti: Il corso è gestito dal Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (CLA, cla@unibs.it) dell’Università degli Studi di Brescia che offre gratuitamente sia le attività di formazione sia l’erogazione di una prova finale (scritta e orale) accompagnata dall’assegnazione di un OPEN BADGE FINALE, denominato ‘C1 English’. Le attività formative offerte dal CLA forniscono agli studenti le competenze linguistiche proprie dell’ INGLESE C1 - QUADRO COMUNE EUROPEO, ossia rispondono pienamente ai parametri di livello C1 previsti dal Quadro comune europeo di riferimento per le lingue, e in particolare porta lo studente ad essere in grado di : 1) comprendere un'ampia gamma di testi lunghi e impegnativi e di riconoscerne il significato implicito; 2) esprimersi in modo fluido e spontaneo senza ricercare le espressioni troppo ovvie; 3) usare la lingua in modo flessibile ed efficace per scopi sociali, accademici e professionali; 4) produrre testi chiari, ben strutturati e dettagliati su argomenti complessi, mostrando un uso controllato di modelli organizzativi, connettori e dispositivi di coesione.Le attività proposte e i contenuti affrontati riguardano sia la pratica della comunicazione scritta e orale, sia l’analisi delle modalità di espressione scritta e orale di testi di livello finale C1.

data.Obiettivi formativi: Obiettivo delle esercitazioni di lingua inglese erogate dal CLA è il raggiungimento del livello C1 definito dal “Quadro di Riferimento Europeo delle Lingue” (https://www.lingueculture.net/wp content/uploads/2021/02/Volume-complementare-QCER2020.pdf). Al termine del corso, lo studente sarà in grado di: 1) comprendere un’ampia gamma di testi complessi e piuttosto lunghi e ricavarne anche il significato implicito. 2) esprimersi in modo scorrevole e spontaneo, senza un eccessivo sforzo per ricercare le parole. 3) usare la lingua in modo flessibile ed efficace per scopi sociali, accademici e professionali. 4) produrre testi chiari, ben strutturati e articolati su argomenti complessi, mostrando di saper controllare le strutture discorsive, i connettivi e i meccanismi di coesione.Tale attività formativa pertanto fornisce gli strumenti metodologici fondamentali per:1. conoscere le strategie e le tecniche della comunicazione in lingua inglese (livello C1 CEFR);2. essere capace di applicarli nella comprensione e produzione di testi di natura specialistica;3. saper comunicare su temi di natura generale in inglese a livello C1; 4. saper argomentare oralmente a livello C1 su temi basilari di settori specialistici e/o professionalizzanti.CONOSCENZE E CAPACITÀ DI COMPRENSIONEAlla fine dell’attività formativa lo studente conosce le basi terminologiche e le strutture linguistico-comunicative (livello C1) necessarie a comprendere testi scritti e orali generali e/o specialistici.CONOSCENZA E CAPACITÀ DI COMPRENSIONE APPLICATE Alla fine dell’attività formativa lo studente conosce ed è in grado di interpretare testi scritti e orali generali e/o specialistici (di livello C1). E’ altresì in grado di utilizzare tali conoscenze per elaborare testi scritti e orali di livello C1.AUTONOMIA DI GIUDIZIOAlla fine del corso lo studente sa individuare i metodi più appropriati per analizzare testi in lingua inglese di livello C1 di ambito generale e/o specialistico.ABILITA’ COMUNICATIVEAlla fine del corso lo studente sa descrivere in lingua inglese, in forma scritta e orale, con accuratezza e appropriatezza di linguaggio, concetti basilari (livello C1) relativi a una delle aree semantiche previste da tale livello di competenza dal Common European Framework.CAPACITA’ DI APPRENDERE (LEARNING SKILLS)Alla fine del corso lo studente è in grado di applicare le conoscenze linguistiche e le metodologie glottodidattiche acquisite a contesti e contenuti generali e academici diversi da quelli acquisiti nel corso, e sa approfondire in autonomia tematiche nuove.
data.Prerequisiti: Gli studenti devono possedere almeno un livello minimo B2 di partenza, non certificato ma autodichiarato all’atto dell’inizio delle attività.
data.Metodi didattici: Lezioni a distanza, coordinate dal CLA, svolte su piattaforma Microsoft Teams e Moodle, previa iscrizione a tale servizio presso il CLA stesso, sono organizzate per fornire i fondamenti per la padronanza delle abilità linguistico-comunicative e pragmatico-linguistiche necessarie a comprendere e produrre testi in lingue inglese di livello C1.Le lezioni sono intese ad implementare: 1) la comprensione e produzione scritta (grammatica e approfondimenti lessicali), 2) la pratica della comprensione scritta e orale (con approfondimenti su tecniche di comprensione, sintesi e rielaborazione del testo).
data.Altro: 1) OPEN BADGE ‘C1 ENGLISH’: Lo studente che supera l'esame finale di questo corso ha diritto all'assegnazione di un OPEN BADGE (open badge https://bestr.it/badge/show/2548), dal titolo ‘C1 ENGLISH’);2) CONTATTI CON IL DOCENTE: Il docente può essere contattato via mail tramite l’indirizzo e-mail del CLA (cla@unibs.it) ed indicando nome e cognome, matricola, corso di laurea e anno di frequenza. 3) RICONOSCIMENTO CERTIFICATI EQUIPARABILI: l'attestazione C1 CLA è equiparabile ai certificati linguistici (di livello C1) riconosciuti dal Dipartimento di Economia e Management ed elencati nella sezione “Certificazioni Linguistiche” del sito dell’università https://www.unibs.it/sites/default/files/2023-01/New%20ultima%20CCSA%20Delibera%20n.%2010.6-2%20del%2015.12.2022%20%20ALLEGATO%20-%20certificazioni%20linguistiche.pdf.Tali certificati devono essere stati conseguiti entro il limite di validità di tre anni prima dell’iscrizione ed essere consegnati presso la Segreteria Studenti. Nel caso di possesso di una certificazione equiparabile lo studente non potrà ricevere l'open badge C1 English del CLA.STUDENTI NON FREQUENTANTI: Il programma per gli studenti non frequentanti è lo stesso di quello per gli studenti frequentanti. Si consiglia agli studenti di contattare il CLA (cla@unibs.it) segnalando l’impossibilità a frequentare.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: La prova finale prevede lo svolgimento di una prova scritta e una prova orale da svolgere senza l’ausilio di dizionari o altri materiali. Per accedere all'orale la prova scritta deve essere superata con una percentuale del 70%. Le due prove devono essere state sostenute e superate nelle due date separate (scritto/orale) dello stesso appello d’esame. Al superamento dell’esame, lo studente ha diritto all’assegnazione di un’attestazione digitale (open badge) denominata ‘C1 English’: https://bestr.it/badge/show/2548?ln=it. 1. PROVA SCRITTA: La prova scritta (60 minuti), su piattaforma Moodle, da sostenersi A DISTANZA, previa iscrizione nelle modalità comunicate e previste nel sito del CLA (https://www.unibs.it/it/ateneo/organizzazione/centro-linguistico-di-ateneo/formazione-linguistica-studenti/attestazione-di-livello-cla-lingua-inglese/attestazione-cla-c1) è tesa a valutare le capacità di comprensione orale e di comprensione/produzione scritta a livello C1. La prova scritta si articola in 4 parti: • GRAMMAR AND VOCABULARY 48/100 (modalità multiple choice, quesiti di livello C1)• READING COMPREHENSION 20/100 (modalità multiple choice, difficoltà C1)• LISTENING COMPREHENSION 20/100 (modalità multiple choice a partire da un testo della durata di 3 min, di livello C1)• WRITING 12/100 ("a 200-word text, based on the information given. Task types include formal emails, reports, and academic essays").Ulteriori dettagli sono disponibili nella pagina del CLA dedicata: https://www.unibs.it/sites/default/files/2023-04/descrizione%20prova%20C1.pdf. 2. PROVA ORALE: La prova orale, della durata di 10 minuti, A DISTANZA, previo superamento dello scritto e su convocazione a coppia con un altro studente in aula Microsoft Teams, include due compiti, come segue: Task 1: Introductory questions e.g.: What do you do in your spare time? Where did you go on holiday last summer? What are your plans for the future? Task 2: Discussion Task: the examiner will present you with a topic to discuss with your partner, to test your interaction and negotiation skills e.g. What kind of factors might affect a person’s decision to move to a foreign country? What kind of factors might a person take into account when planning a holiday? La valutazione dell’orale tiene conto della efficienza dei metodi utilizzati, della completezza ed esattezza delle risposte, della pronuncia e fluency, nonché della chiarezza nella presentazione di fatti, pensieri e opinioni.Il superamento della prova non dà seguito ad un punteggio finale ma all’assegnazione dell’open badge ‘C1 English’, raggiungibile con il 70% dei punti dello scritto e dall’esito positivo della prova orale.
data.Programma esteso: La bibliografia suggerita e i materiali condivisi dal docente durante le ore di lezione convergono alla trattazione dei seguenti temi:1) la comprensione di un discorso lungo anche se non chiaramente strutturato e con riferimenti e contenuti impliciti; 2) la comprensione senza troppo sforzo di trasmissioni televisive e film; 3) la comprensione di testi letterari e informativi lunghi e complessi; 4) le differenze di stile; 5) i testi specialistici e le istruzioni tecniche lunghe, anche quando non appartengono al proprio ambito di studio e/o ricerca;6) il parlato spontaneo; 7) l’uso della lingua in modo flessibile ed efficace nelle relazioni sociali e professionali; 8) l’espressione di idee e opinioni chiara e precisa; 9) le descrizioni chiare e articolate su argomenti complessi, integrate con sotto-argomenti, sviluppate in più punti e concluse in modo appropriato;10) la scrittura di testi chiari e ben strutturati sviluppando analiticamente il proprio punto di vista; 11) le lettere, i saggi e le relazioni di argomenti complessi; 12) lo stile accademico.

data.Contenuti: The aim of the course is to provide a comprehensive overview of the European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), its principles, its rules, its method of implementation, its risk-based approach and the activity of the institutions it addresses. The analysis will focus on the pivotal concept of "accountability" of data controllers, the real keystone of the brand new legal order on data protection, which specifically requires aware and responsible actors.The presentation of practical cases demonstrating the need to manage data protection compliance within a strict regulatory framework will allow students to practically develop an intuitive sensitivity to data protection compliance as one of the most valuable strategic assets of a company. Data governance consists of the ability to both extract and interpret salient information, but above all to be able to account for one's choices from the design of data processing, in order to minimise the risk of unnecessary or disruptive interference with personal data and privacy.Another objective of the course is to understand the different approaches to regulating data flows held by the EU's foreign trading partners and how the deep conceptual distinction between 'privacy' and 'data protection' still influences them.
data.Testi: Course materials will be reported in class
data.Obiettivi formativi: Knowledge and understanding:At the end of the course, students should be able to:- know the principles and concepts applicable to data ownership and processing;- follow continuous engineering innovation in data processing and understand the significant features of relevant technologies such as the application of big data and artificial intelligence technologies in different sectors;- master the tools and institutions compatible with the new legal framework governing data protection.Application of knowledge:At the end of the study programme, students will be able to:- assess the impact of data processing on the rights and freedoms of data subjects;- elaborate and plan different privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default solutions depending on the specific purposes and situations of processing;- communicate and work effectively as an expert in data protection issues.Judgement skills:At the end of the study programme, students will be able to:- apply the rules set out in specific data processing schemes;- recognise the data protection risks within a processing operation and identify appropriate and effective measures to minimise them- prepare original reports and impact assessments of specific data processing simulations.Communication skills:On completion of the programme of study, students will be able to:- develop the ability to communicate in written form through exercises and in oral form through classroom interaction and debate;- use the knowledge and communication of data protection legislation; and- develop the ability to provide legal advice to data controllers and data processors.Learning skills:At the end of the curriculum, students will be able to:- build an analytical toolbox from data protection and privacy legislation;- solve problems in dynamic contexts and develop critical positions.
data.Prerequisiti: Private law basic notions
data.Metodi didattici: Classroom-taught lesson, attendance recommended
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: The exam consists of an oral exam, which is compulsory for all students, and which focuses on the course programme as it is carried out in the textbook adopted for teaching and in the teaching materials made available to students. The grade will be expressed in thirtieth.The evaluation criteria are understanding of legal notions, ability to analyse, mastery of legal vocabulary, ability to connect.
data.Programma esteso: Context and framework of European data protection lawDifferences between right to privacy and right to data protectionFrom the Parent Directive to the Regulation (GDPR)- "personal data"- Special categories of data ("sensitive data")- "data processing"- subjects of data governanceThe principles of the GDPR- lawfulness, fairness and transparency of processing- purpose limitation- data minimisation- accuracy, storage limitation and security- accountability- conditions for lawfulness of processing and special categories of data- security measures- management of data breaches- accountability rules- compliance tools- data protection by design and by default- DPIASupervisory authorities- powers and sanctions- the European Data Protection Board- the right to be informed- the rights of rectification, restriction and objection- the 'right to be forgotten- the rights against automated decision-making, including profiling- respect of individuals' rights- EU-US agreements on data flowsEU Data Strategy 2020- ePrivacy Regulation- the AI RegulationSpecific types of personal data and their protection rules- health data- genetic and biometric data- data processing for research and statistical purposesContemporary challenges in personal data protection:- big data, algorithms and AI- Web 2.0 and social networks- Web 3.0 and IoT- the Big Tech problem

data.Contenuti: The Laboratory aims to provide the knowledge useful to make students autonomous in the use of geospatial data in the context of the analysis of social and socio-economic phenomena and for business purposes such as geomarketing. In the first part of the course the main types of georeferenced data (vectors, polygons and raster) will be presented, and the main concepts of distance and connectivity in space (matrices of spatial weights) will be defined. Then, in the second part, the focus will be on analysis of the spatial data. In this regard, the aim is to present the main methods for manipulating georeferenced data and for analysing discrete georeferenced data that include the Exploratory Spatial Data Analysis (ESDA), cross-sectional and panel spatial regression models to deal with spatial autocorrelation and regression models capable of managing spatial heterogeneity (Geographically Weighted Reegression, GWR). For the practical implementation of these models, open source software such as R, Geoda, GeoDaSpace, GWR4 will be used.
data.Testi: • Francisco Rowe and Dani Arribas-Bel: Spatial Modelling for Data Scientists https://gdsl-ul.github.io/san/• Michael Dorman: Introduction to Spatial Data Programming with R https://geobgu.xyz/r/index.html• Robin Lovelace, Jakub Nowosad, Jannes Muenchow: Geocomputation with R https://bookdown.org/robinlovelace/geocompr/• Taro Mieno: R as GIS for Economists https://tmieno2.github.io/R-as-GIS-for-Economists/
data.Obiettivi formativi: a) Knowledge and understanding (KN)The aim of the laboratory is to provide the knowledge for identifing the main types of spatial data and to properly analyse te latter. During the laboratory the students will learn ad-hoc software such as Geoda, GeoDaSpace and GWR and the main R packages for Geographical Information Science (GIS) and spatial econometrics.b) Applying knowledge and understanding (AKN)Students will be able to develop the empirical skills needed to analyse georeferenced data. They will learn to search for data online, to develop their own R scripts, and to use the most common econometric methods to analyse data.c) Making judgements (MJ)The students will have developed the ability to understand and critically interpret the main results of their analyses. Furthermore, they will be able to read and understand specialized articles that make use spatial econometric techniques and to make judgements about their results.d) Communication skills (CS)The students will be able to communicate using the appropriate lexicon to different interlocutors. They will write and present a team project in class, and they will have to demonstrate to be able to reply to questions made by the teacher and other students.e) Learning skills (LS)The students will reach the ability to learn autonomously what techniques have to be used according to the context of analysis an of the type of spatial data they handle. Furthermore, they will learn academic writing, to work in team in a project with a deadline, and to expose in public the results of their research
data.Prerequisiti: Knowledge of R programming language and of the basic econometric/statistical analysis
data.Metodi didattici: Students will actively work on a group project assigned by the teacher. It is recommended to be equipped with their personal notebook during the lessons.
data.Altro: The reception hours are as follows:Monday from 13.30 to 14.30.Tuesday from 13.30 to 14.30.It is required to send an email to book the reception.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: Students' final evaluation of knowledge (KN), applied knowledge (AKN), making judgements (MJ), learning (LS) and communication skills (CS) is based on two components:1) a written paper (group work) with the aim of applying the acquired knowledge to a case study related to the field of geomarketing, transports, land use, environment, social science (poverty, migration, economic growth), etc. Students will have to analyse georeferenced data by means of charts, maps and by using spatial econometric tools [(KN), (AKN), (LS)].2) Presentation of the paper in class by the group [(AKN), (CS)]].
data.Programma esteso: The following contents will be addressed:• Spatial data types• Visualization of spatial data• Spatial data operations• Geometry operations• Handling raster and netCDF data• Exploratory Spatial Data Analysis (ESDA)• Spatial econometrics: spatial dependence in cross-sectional data• Spatial econometrics: spatial heterogeneity in cross-sectional data• Spatial econometrics: spatial dependence in panel dataAttendance is highly recommended.

data.Contenuti: Each lesson contains detailed content that students can find in the extended Program and in the slides provided by the teacher. Here you find a summary. Numbers relate to Chapters of the textbook.1. Introduction to International Economics.2. An overview of World Trade.3. Labor Productivity and Comparative Advantage: the Ricardian Model.4. Specific Factors and Income Distribution.5. Resources and Trade: the Heckscher-Ohlin Model.6. The Standard Trade Model.7. External Economies of Scale and the International Location of Production.8. Firms in the Global Economy: Export Decisions, Outsourcing, and Multinational Enterprises.9. The Instruments of Trade Policy.10. The Political Economy of Trade Policy.11. Trade Policy in Developing Countries.12. Controversies in Trade Policy.22. Developing countries: growth, crisis, and reform.
data.Testi: Paul Krugman, Maurice Obstfeld, Marc Melitz; International Economics: Theory and Policy (11th edition, global edition); Pearson; 2018; 978-1-292-21487-0;Capitoli 1-12, first part of 22.There is the possibility of obtaining a free open access copy at https://www.academia.edu/45169893/International_Economics_Theory_and_Policy_Global_Edition_by_Paul_R_Krugman_Maurice_Obstfeld_Marc_J_Melitz The new edition (12th edition, 2022) of the same book is available at https://www.pearson.com/uk/educators/higher-education-educators/program/Krugman-International-Economics-Theory-and-Policy-Global-Edition-12th-Edition/PGM100003100497.html In this edition there are updated examples and case studies: i) the impacts of Brexit and COVID-19 (Chapter 7)ii) firms' global sourcing decisions and the new USMCA treaty (Chapter 8)iii) US-China trade tensions (Chapter 10)iv) the effects of the Trump trade war on global trade and the COVID-19 pandemic (Chapter 19)v) the Dec. 2020 EU-UK trade deal plus the prior withdrawal agreement and its implications for the Irish border (Chapter 21)vi) euro area policy innovations in response to COVID-19 (Chapter 21)We'll go through some of these new issues via bibliographic material supplied in the Comunità Didattica. Digital tools (optional):www.MyEconLab.comFurther readings:Few readings and other material will be distributed in class and on-line, via Moodle platform "Comunità didattica" International Economics (A.A. 2022), regarding special issues and papers related to International Trade and Policy program.
data.Obiettivi formativi: a) Knowledge and understanding (KN)The students will be able to elaborate complex theoretical concepts regarding international economics, such as e.g. the absolute advantage and the comparative advantage (who trades what with whom and why), and the terms of trade. They will learn to solve models where resource distribution and use determine the pattern of trade, or where the market structure determines intra-industry trade. They will be able to identify gains from trade, what kind of policies countries apply and their effect on good prices and society welfare, and why developing countries have a different perspective about trade policy. They will deal with many case studies at hand.b) Applying knowledge and understanding (AKN)The students face empirical problems as well, especially regarding the evaluation of correlations and relationships between international trade aggregates on specific relevant topics, such as international competition (relative wages and productivity), the Leontieff paradox (skill-content of US imports and technologically-advanced trading partners), the double-causality effect of the crises. In order to achieve this objective, students learn to manage on-line databases, searching for adequate data, posing a research question, developing a method to get results and answering with complete and convincing conclusions.c) Making judgements (MJ)The students learn to formulate theoretically and empirically based arguments about past and current events of international trade such as why countries exchange goods, services or assets, what is the role of WTO in setting rules and solving disputes, and why countries need such an institution. Moreover, they can explain why policymakers today engage into applying tariffs and subsidies, especially in crucial sectors of the economy, and whether this is beneficial to trading countries. They learn to make judgements about the benefits or drawbacks of free trade, protectionism, and other levels of economic integration.d) Communication skills (CS)The students are required to present a team project in a poster session, in order to deliver one’s own abilities in communicating international trade concepts to a mixed (experts and not) audience in English. Moreover, students will be asked to discuss in class their own solutions to three home assignments.e) Learning skills (LS)This course gives a set of learning instruments that include homework problems to solve individually, the possibility to identify a research question and implement academic writing skills on a teamwork structured project with a deadline, and to make use of algebraic and graphic techniques to answer specific questions regarding international economics issues.
data.Prerequisiti: Pre-requisites:Students must have a good knowledge of Principles of Micro and Macroeconomics (undergraduate level), General Mathematics and English language. Proficiency in English is useful but not required.
data.Metodi didattici: It is advisable, even if not obligatory, to attend each lecture, because the course requires students’ active learning.The teacher takes notice of whom is attending each lecture. Only a presence of 75% or more (at least 18 lectures) gives a student the status of "attending student".Only attending students (either on-site or on-line) participate to active learning: homework, discussion and final poster session.THE REST OF THE STUDENTS WILL BE CONSIDERED NON-ATTENDING.Non-attending students are required to study the textbook, reading all the material uploaded on Moodle platform "Comunità Didattica" International Economics (A.A. 2022), and take the final test in the official dates of exam. Example of past tests or exercises will be available in the Comunità Didattica at the end of the course.Optionally, students might study over the digital tool www.MyEconLab.com to get acquainted with interactive graphics, questions, and all the material in the required chapters.AS FAR AS ATTENDING STUDENTS, their final evaluation of knowledge (KN), applied knowledge (AKN), making judgements (MJ), learning (LS) and communication skills (CS) about IE is based on three components:1) Students are required to solve INDIVIDUALLY home assignments and critically discuss the solution in class [testing for (AKN), (MJ)] with a maximum of three homework (valued 2 points each). Students allowed by the dean of the Department to connect at distance can discuss their homework over the MS Teams platform, sharing their screen.2) By December, students will prepare a POSTER on a topic of their choice (from a list of topics provided by the teacher) and present it in a POSTER SESSION, to experiment COMMUNICATION techniques related to International Economics. THIS IS A TEAM WORK; the teacher will set each team and evaluate both the team work and each individual capacity/knowledge [testing for (AKN), (LS), (CS)].More details and instructions will be given at the beginning of the course.3) Final test. Students are required to answer theoretical open questions and solve for exercises [testing for (KN), (MJ), (LS)]. The test dates are officially set by the calendar of the Department.WARNING: IF THE EMERGENCY OF THE PANDEMIC WILL INTENSIFY DURING THE SEMESTER, BOTH THE POSTER SESSION AND FINAL LECTURES WILL BE GIVEN ON-LINE, AT DISTANCE, OVER THE MS TEAMS PLATFORM.
data.Altro: Students are expected to attend the lectures, to study the main textbook, looking at the slides, to solve for home assignments, and read suggested readings for in-depth analysis.RULES FOR NON ATTENDING STUDENTS OR THE LATE-COMERS:Slides will be distributed to facilitate comprehension of the subject via the Moodle platform Comunità Didattica International Economics (A.A. 2022).Office hours and email are available tools to contact the teacher.They MAY start a forum on Moodle platform Comunità Didattica IE to get answers from the Community of the other students and the teacher.They HAVE access to past exams on Moodle platform Comunità Didattica IE.They MUST take the final test (at official dates) to pass the exam.Their final grade is based on the final test only. The test is based on four questions, two of them are exercises and two are theoretical questions on the models.In exceptional, serious and rare cases, the teacher (at her discretion) might allow non attending students to take an oral exam after the written test.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: ATTENDING students' final evaluation of knowledge (KN), applied knowledge (AKN), making judgements (MJ), learning (LS) and communication skills (CS) about IE is based on three components:1) Each student solves INDIVIDUALLY home assignments (exercises or data analysis with graphs and tables) and briefly but critically discusses the solution in class [testing for (AKN), (MJ)] for a maximum of three homework.2) By December, students prepare a POSTER on a topic of their choice (from a list provided by the teacher) and present it in a POSTER SESSION, to experiment COMMUNICATION techniques related to International Economics. This is a TEAM work, and the teacher sets each team. An evaluation of the work is given to the team and to each individual student [testing for (AKN), (MJ), (LS), (CS)].More details and instructions are provided at the beginning of the course.3) Written Final Test. Each student answers two theoretical and two technical questions, solving for exercises, about international economics [testing for (KN), (AKN), (LS)].Assessment method:[Weight] of each requested activities in the final evaluation:[20%]: 1) Total Homework.[50%]: 2) Poster session active contribution and participation at the end of the course.[30%]: 3) Written final test at the end of the course (at official dates).A positive final grade goes from a minimum (Italian grade system) of 18 points (D, in the Anglo-Saxon grade system) to 30 points (A). If the total evaluation is less than 18 (F) the preparation is not considered adequate and the student needs to re-take the written test (only). In some cases, for excellent preparation, a student may get 30 points 'cum laude' (A+).NON-ATTENDING students are evaluated only [100%] on their performance in the Final Test, which is an extended version of the final test for attending students. The Italian grading system applies.
data.Programma esteso: Extended Program:1. Introduction to International Economics.What is International Economics about?The gains from trade.The pattern of trade.How much trade.The Balance of Payment.Exchange rate determination.International Policy coordination.The International Capital market.2. An overview of World Trade.Size matters! The Gravity Model.Impediments to trade: distance, barriers, borders.Has the world gotten smaller?What do we trade?3. Labor Productivity and Comparative Advantage: the Ricardian Model.We build a model to explain how trade takes place.Production functions and the resource constraint. Deriving the Production Possibility Frontier (PPF), the scale parameter and MRT in a country.Assumptions on labor input requirement and productivity in two countries.An absolute advantage explanation of the gains from trade.One-factor Ricardian model: assumptions, derivation and solution.Comparative advantage and pattern of trade.Case study: War of the Roses.Opportunity cost of producing and MRT.Formal definition of Comparative Advantage (CA).Specialization.4. Specific Factors and Income Distribution.The specific factors model.What is a specific factor?International trade in the specific factors model.Income distribution and the gains from trade.5. Resources and Trade: the Heckscher-Ohlin Model.Two-factors Heckscher-Ohlin Model.Factor endowment, Capital and Labor.Price of factors: returns to labor and capital.Preferences.Technology.Factor returns with free trade.Two resource constraints and derivation of the PPF.Numerical example.Substitutability in factor inputs and the concavity of the PPF.Isovalue line and optimal production.Relative Prices and the pattern of trade.The declining labor share.Empirical evidence of the HO model.6. The Standard Trade Model.A standard model of a Trading Economy.Production Possibilities and Relative Supply.Relative Prices and Demand.The Welfare effects of changes in the terms of trade.Determining relative prices.7. External Economies of Scale and the International Location of Production.Economies of scale and international trade.Economies of scale and the market structure.The theory of external economies.Interregional trade.8. Firms in the Global Economy: Export Decisions, Outsourcing, and Multinational Enterprises.The theory of imperfect competition.Monopolistic competition and trade.Intra-industry trade.Trade costs and export decisions.Dumping.Horizontal and vertical FDI.Trade-offs in FDI, outsourcing, offshoring.9. The Instruments of Trade Policy.Import tariffs, customs duties.Case study: Steel Industry in the US in 2001.Case study: EU trade policy.Export tariffs.Case study: Pakistan raw cotton tax in 1988.Type of tariff: ad valorem or specific tariff.When a small importing country imposes a tariff: graphical representation, equilibrium prices, welfare effects.When Two countries trading one product: imposition of a tariff, graphical representation, international equilibrium price, who trades with whom.Quotas and subsidies.10. The Political Economy of Trade Policy.The case for free trade.National welfare argument against free trade.Income distribution and trade policy.International negotiations and trade policy.the History of GATT.Case study: Banana Republic: trade dispute over bananas.Free Trade Areas: NAFTA.The degree of economic integration, regional integration in the world and free trade areas.Do agricultural subsidies hurt the third world?Other Trade policies: Government procurement, export credit subsidies, regulation.Summarizing the effect of alternative trade policies.11. Trade Policy in Developing Countries.Import-substituting industrialization.The infant industry argument.Case study: Mexico.Trade liberalization since 1985.India's boom.12. Controversies in Trade Policy.Technology and externalities.Imperfect competition and strategic trade policy.Globalization and low-wage labor.Globalization and the environment.22. Developing countries: Growth, Crisis, and Reform.Income, wealth, and growth in the World Economy.The Gap between Rich and Poor.Has the world income gap narrowed over time?The importance of developing countries for global growth.Structural features of developing countries.

data.Contenuti: The course introduces the students to the basic principles that guide corporate managers and entrepreneurs in making their ordinary and extraordinary financing decisions in national and international companies. It also provides the analytical tools to operate in the financing and investing area.Topics covered include: financial analysis, cash flow estimation, time value of money, capital budgeting, the relationship between risk and return, cost of capital, capital structure decisions, company's valuation.
data.Testi: Vernimmen Pierre, Corporate finance. Theory and practice, 2018, 5th ed. John Wiley&Sons, ISBN 978-1-119-42448-2 - also available as an e-book on wiley.comIt is suggested to read the whole book. In any case the following chapters will not be used in the final test: 6, 7, 24, 25, 43 and 51.
data.Obiettivi formativi: 1. Knowledge and understandingThe course introduces the students to the basic principles of financing and investing decisions, providing the analytical tools for assessing company’s financial situation and company's value.The aim is to provide students with a thorough understanding of techniques, theories and issues found in practical corporate finance situations.2. Applying knowledge and understandingThe objective of the course is to strengthen the knowledge of the principles of finance with the aim of providing students with the know-how required to operate as managers or entrepreneurs within an international company.At the end of the course the student will be able to:a. realize a financial analysis and determine the company’s financial situationb. conduct a capital budgeting analysisc. identify the future financial needs of the companyd. evaluate the financial debt sustainability and the company’s capital structuree. identify the company’s value according to the DCF model and the market3. Making judgementsAt the end of the course the student will be able to derive financial information from the company financial reporting and thus will be in a position to analyze and provide practical guidance to Senior Management4. Communication skillsThe student will be able to communicate with financial intermediaries and consultants in an effective way, leveraging on the industry language5. Learning skillsBy interacting with the professor, by solving exercises and working through case studies, the student will learn to analyze and evaluate the most often encountered financial problems in today’s companies. Emphasis is set on a proactive way to address problems.
data.Prerequisiti: No specific previous knowhow is mandatory except from the ones required by the Degree Program.
data.Metodi didattici: The course will alternate theoretical teaching – face to face lectures - and practical sessions on corporate cases and exercises to allow students to apply the concepts illustrated during classes.
data.Verifica dell'apprendimento: At the end of the course the exam will be a written test (exercises, open and multiple-choice questions) on the topics covered during the course. The test is closed book. A non-programmable calculator is allowed.There is a 30 point grading scale with highest result being 30/30 and pass result 18/30.Assessment: Final Mark

The time value of money. Compounding and discounting.6. Investment analysis and valuation criteriaSection 3 – Cost of capital7. Risk and return. Portfolio theory and The Capital Asset Pricing Model8. data.Contenuti: The course deals with extensions of the classical topics of International Economics. In particular, the focus is on the economy of European integration, analysing through instruments of international economics, the economic development in the Eurozone, the impact of the financial crisis, major changes in policies and European legislation, the potential impact of the Trans-Atlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP), the effect of enlargement of the European Union, as well as the impact of Brexit. Lastly, recent policies and financial instruments set to face the Covid-19 emergency are included in the course. These include the EU Solidarity Fund, the Support to mitigate Unemployment Risks in an Emergency (SURE), and the Recovery Fund. The theoretical part is accompanied by the analysis of recent policy agendas like the von der Leyen Commission's priorities for 2019-2024 and the EU greed deal.
data.Testi: Baldwin, R. and C. Wyplosz, "The Economics of European Integration", Mc Graw Hill Education, Fifth Edition 2015, ISBN-13 9780077169657; ISBN-10 0077169654Molle W. “European Cohesion Policy”, Routledge, 2007, ISBN-10: 0415438128; ISBN-13: 978-0415438124John B, Berkowitz P., Hardy S., Muravska T. (a cura di) “EU Cohesion Policy: Reassessing performance and direction”, Routledge, First Edition 2016, ISBN-10: 1138224642; ISBN-13: 978-1138224643Bénassy-Quéré A., and di Mauro B.W., Europe in the Time of Covid-19, CEPR Press 2020, ISBN: 978-1-912179-33-6
data.Obiettivi formativi: a) Knowledge and understanding (KN)The aim of the course is to deepen the knowledge of international economics, applying the main concepts previously acquired to understand the process of European integration under an economic and institutional perspective. Students will be able to identify the main steps of European integration, the macroeconomics of monetary integration, micro policies and the macroeconomics of monetary integration. Furthermore, recent policy strategies like the von der Leyen Commission's priorities for 2019-2024, the EU green deal and tools like the EU Solidarity Fund and Support to mitigate Unemployment Risks in an Emergency (SURE) will be discussed.The course is based on the text "The Economics of European Integration" and the material provided by the teacher.b) Applying knowledge and understanding (AKN)Students will be able to face the topics covered in the course developing the empirical skills needed to check for empirical relation between the data. They will learn to search for data online, to develop a research question, and to use basic econometric tools to analyse data and to draw convincing conclusions.c) Making judgements (MJ)The students will have developed the ability to understand and critically interpret the main economic events in the light of the knowledge acquired during the course. They will be able to read and understand specialized articles (for example from voxeu.org) and to make judgements about the economic policy proposals in the public debate.d) Communication skills (CS)The students will be able to communicate using the appropriate lexicon to different interlocutors. They will write and present a team project in class, and they will have to demonstrate to be able to reply to questions made by the teacher and other students.e) Learning skills (LS)The students will reach the ability to learn autonomously complex economic concepts that will allow them to understand specialized news and articles. Furthermore, they will learn academic writing, to work in team in a project with a deadline, and to empirically analyse data.
data.Prerequisiti: International Economics
